tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

# Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | — (2K only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

## Rule 3: Determine Output Format BEFORE Generating
target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

## Rule 4: Identify the Use Case, Then Confirm with User
Determine which scenario below best matches, present a suggested plan to the user, and confirm before executing. When a request spans several scenarios (e.g. A then L), combine their steps and confirm the combined plan.

---

## Scenario A: 3D Printing (white model)
Trigger: user mentions print, slicer, figurine, miniature, statue, physical model — single-color.
Suggested flow:
1. Detect installed slicers (meshy_send_to_slicer, slicer_type:"auto") — present list, save for later
2. Generate an untextured model with target_formats:["obj"]: meshy_text_to_3d (preview), or meshy_image_to_3d with should_texture:false
3. Wait for completion
4. Optionally check printability (meshy_analyze_printability, free). If it reports errors, either repair with model_url = the generation task's OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) so the result stays OBJ — on that route pass printer_type and intended_print_longest_side_mm, since intended_print_height_mm only works with task / GLB input — or repair by the analyze task, then meshy_convert the repaired GLB to obj (1 credit). print_ready only fixes OBJ
5. Download the OBJ (the repair task's, if repaired) with print_ready=true and print_height_mm (local Z-up fix and scaling)

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

# Re-review rulings — 2026-10-27 (delegated: the user said "just use best judgment")

Marker for every edit that applies one of these: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling Rn)*.
In-text record where a decision is stated: "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling Rn (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): ..."
These rulings never reverse a prior user ruling; they settle consequences the user's rulings left ambiguous or unimplementable.

## General rules (G)
- G1 Owner wins: where two GDDs disagree on a value, field, unit or contract, the registry `source:` GDD wins and the other conforms. If the thing is unregistered, the PUBLISHER of the field/signal/value wins and the consumer conforms.
- G2 Specialist disagreements: follow the creative-director's stated resolution in that GDD's disagreements list. Where the CD said "the user should choose", take the CD's stated lean.
- G3 Carried-over blockers (flagged "still not fixed"/"carried over"): previous edits did not land. After each edit, Grep for the old wording and confirm it is gone everywhere in the GDD (body, examples, ACs, tuning tables, OQs).
- G4 ACs that contradict the GDD's own formulas: recompute from the formula at registry defaults; never weaken a formula to match an AC.
- G5 Division/overflow at boundaries: guard explicitly (e.g. avail == 0 -> share 0, everything unserved); state the guard in the formula and add a boundary AC.

## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. Update the kernel seq ACs (L883, L892, L902-904) and PC-7 together.
- R3 Completion sentinel (kernel CR-19b). Every owner callable receives `ctx`; results flow through ctx, never the return value: validate reports via ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason); snapshot via ctx.put(payload); apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx). Every callable's only return is `return ctx.complete()` (a typed token). No `-> void` owner callables.
- R4 Mouse aim. The Player Controller's form is canonical: cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre) / k_eff, where f_q is the quantized camera position actually used for the frame. The Pipeline PUBLISHES f_q. Aim direction = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN, with AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y) (ruling D10); remove the chest-based subtraction from the Pipeline's D.14b/D.7. Cursor units: the fixer must VERIFY the unit of the cursor source (e.g. Viewport.get_mouse_position() under the Pipeline's canvas_items stretch wiring (ii)) against docs/engine-reference/godot/ and the Pipeline's own wiring text, then make the label, the variable table and the divisor agree in both GDDs; if the reference cannot settle it, mark the unit claim [UNV] and add an in-engine verification AC.
- R5 Carry tell (consequence of X3). Owners: Attention owns the intake numbers and the ONE integrator (Attention's walk-in convention and tick accounting are canonical; Boarding quotes them); Boarding owns the live-choice acceptance (AC-BS-123) and its K definitions, stated with Attention's integrator; Derelict owns the route length (21-28 tiles, X3). Scope: the burden applies only to SALVAGE carry — an item carried that was picked up inside a non-home locus (derelict) — moving or standing, until dropped/installed/thrown; never to carrying at home or of the player's own kit. Pace-robustness, scoped to that salvage carry only: (a) while a salvage carry is held, attention decay is suspended (freezing with cargo is priced, per X3); (b) dropping and re-taking the same item grants no fresh TELL_REARM immunity (the rearm timer keys on the item, not the pickup). Attention may re-derive weights/theta within these scoped rules, but must NOT invent weights to force K3-K5 green: all values stay PLACEHOLDER, and if the live-choice margin cannot be shown on paper with honest numbers, AC-BS-123(d) is re-written as a spike gate (owner, the boarding spike, its pass line), which is the expected outcome.
- R6 Pod statuses (consequence of user ruling D60 "statuses run in the pod"). Suit's reading stands: the reserve drains, the cell drains while lit, source RESERVE. Web Map conforms: delete WM-17b's HOLD reading and close ASK-S2. Pillar-2 mitigation: the valve click plays only on the source TRANSITION edge (once when breath_src becomes RESERVE), never per run. Recompute every pod-leg figure from the registry's own leg formula at registry defaults (ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS default 45, not 180; the registry's formulas use 945 ticks per leg — verify in the registry before using) and state run counts with an explicit floor and a carried remainder so every "exactly N" oracle is an integer.
- R7 PD1 static spill bound (user ruling D31: 'static authored spill <= 24 px'). The bound stays 24 px — it is the user's number. The home ship's spine_corridor (computed 26 px) must be brought within it by Derelict Authoring (light placement, fixture position or corridor dressing — the least invasive change; show the recomputed s <= 24). Lighting's AC-LO-69 stays per-push BLOCKING.
- R8 Units of a request field shared by producer and consumer (e.g. Perception LEVEL vs Audio): G1 — the producer defines the unit; the consumer converts. State the unit in both GDDs with the conversion.
- R9 Undesigned dependencies (VS/Alpha systems with no GDD): not a blocker; keep them listed as "undesigned — provisional contract" with the interface this GDD assumes.
- R10 Pending-confirmation defaults and PLACEHOLDER values are not changed by these rulings unless a blocker shows them internally inconsistent.
- R11 X14 (reference machine) stays OPEN: never name or invent a reference machine, build type or spec anywhere.
# Second delegated rulings — 2026-10-28 (the user: "use your own best judgement, fix the remaining issues, name whatever you need yourself")

Marker for every edit: *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling Rn)* or *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.
In-text record: "Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling Rn (user delegated all remaining calls, including naming the reference machine): ...".
G1-G5 and R1-R10 of rr-rulings.md stay binding except where amended below. R11 (X14 stays open) is SUPERSEDED by R12.

## G6 Cross-GDD edits are now allowed
A blocker that needs a sibling GDD to change is fixed IN the sibling. Owner wins (G1): the registry `source:` GDD, else the publisher of the field/signal, keeps its value; the other conforms. Each file has exactly one writer per pass; requests to another file go to that file's writer.
Classify every blocker first: **CONFLICT** (the same thing has two values/contracts in two GDDs) -> the owner's value stands and the other GDD conforms; **GAP** (the owner lacks a surface, exemption, field or signal that a consumer's user-ruled or delegated-ruled behaviour requires, e.g. Interaction's act_gate exempt list lacking self-patch, HUD lacking a give_up surface) -> the OWNER ADDS it, and the consumer's requirement is the spec. Never "fix" a gap by removing the consumer's ruled behaviour.
Precedence: where R1 text conflicts with R13/R14, R13/R14 win; re-mark such text "delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14".

## R12 Reference machines and build (closes X14; supersedes R11)
- **RM-DESKTOP (minimum-spec desktop):** Windows 10/11 64-bit; 6-core/6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class; 8 GB RAM; GPU of the NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / AMD Radeon RX 570 4 GB class (Vulkan 1.2+); SATA SSD; 1920x1080 at 60 Hz. P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms.
- **RM-DECK (handheld):** Steam Deck LCD (2022), SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz panel, 30 fps target. P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 33.3 ms.
- **Build type for every wall-clock figure:** a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus` (project.godot), vsync on, the pipeline's warm-up of 120 frames, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded with each result.
- **P99 headroom:** pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling (headroom >= 1.7 ms desktop, >= 3.3 ms Deck).
- The developer's machine is not a reference machine; figures from it are indicative only.
- Recorded in `project.yaml` as `qa.min_spec` (done by the orchestrator). In GDDs: replace "X14 open / not named / [blocked: reference hardware]" with the named machines; performance ACs become gated on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK at the spike (still measured at the spike, so a value not yet measured is "pending spike", not "blocked").

## R13 OQ-50: Continue of a Save & Quit keeps the epoch (amends R1)
User ruling D16 ("not steerable by quit") outranks delegated R1. A **death-stub restore** advances `restore_epoch` (durably, R14). A **Continue** that restores a `QUIT` generation which is the newest non-demoted verified generation **carries the epoch unchanged** (no epoch write). A Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback) advances it. ACs: (i) death restore -> e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) Save & Quit, Continue -> same epoch, identical draws; (iii) kill, Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation -> e+1; (iv) same (save, epoch) -> identical draws.

## R14 Where the epoch lives and when it is durable (fixes kernel CR-15 vs SL-23 and the REBASED-key/trailer-SHA defect)
- `restore_epoch` is stored in a **per-slot side file** `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32), written atomically (temp file + rename) by the Save/Load worker. It is **not** in any generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA and every key derived from them never change.
- When an advance is due (R13), Save/Load issues the epoch write in a **pre-restore staging step, before calling `request_restore`**, polls it per frame (never blocks the main thread), and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`. The kernel's LOADING stays atomic within one boundary service. Kernel CR-15 is reworded to: "Save/Load's epoch staging step has completed (EPOCH_DURABLE, or a logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE with save_status = FAILED)", and the kernel lists the failure-path exposure too.
- If the write fails or exceeds `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder), the restore proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway). This is a **listed exposure**: a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once. The ACs for durability are scoped to the success path; the failure path has its own AC (logged, status FAILED, play continues).
- A missing or corrupt `slot_epoch.bin` reads as `max(epoch recorded in the newest generation's header copy, 0) + 1`. Each generation header also records the epoch at write time (read-only copy, for recovery).

## R15 OQ-52: confirmed option (a)
A `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt from the fairness step-back. Confirmed; drop "USER DECISION".

## R16 OQ-DO-30: option (A)
The playtest preset registers only `debug_overlay_mark`; `debug_overlay_reveal` is dev-only. A tester session can never leave `HIDDEN`. Update DO-2/6/8, AC-DO-170, AC-DO-185.

## R17 Interaction OQ 48: confirmed
A wounded victim is not guaranteed an escape (Pillar 3, honest horror). Confirmed; no cooldown or damage floor.

## R18 Player Controller OQ 29(ii): pre-ruled conditional
If the target-acquisition spike fails and the lighter fallbacks do not close the gap, `aim_indicator` defaults ON for mouse players (still player-toggleable). Until then D9 (off by default) stands.

## R19 Boarding OQ-BS-34 fallback: pre-ruled conditional
If the boarding spike finds no K3 pass line inside 21-28 tiles with Attention's levers, the X3 route band's upper end widens to 31 tiles for the reference sortie (lower end stays 21). Not applied now; the spike decides.

## R20 Every "default applied, pending user confirmation" is confirmed
Every item marked "Default applied ... pending user confirmation" or "(confirm)" in any GDD is confirmed as of 2026-10-28 by delegation. Re-mark it "confirmed 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R20" and remove it from open user-decision lists. Do not change the value.

## R21 Remaining "USER DECISION" items
Any other "USER DECISION" left in a GDD is decided by its creative-director lean (G2) or, absent one, by the option that preserves prior user rulings and needs the least new content; record it as delegated ruling R21 with one sentence of reason. Never leave a "USER DECISION" open.

Scope signal: XL
Specialists: none (lean confirming re-review after the cross-GDD fix pass, delegated rulings R12-R21)
Blocking items: 0 | Recommended: 9
Summary: Verdict: APPROVED, with recommended follow-ups. Both prior blockers are resolved, and my spot-checks confirm it. The departure void now holds in web-map-and-transit.md, and AT-10 uses one drained-BURDEN rule that agrees with the state table. Nothing remaining blocks implementation. Every outstanding item is either a stale cross-reference or a fix owned by a sibling GDD under G6. Attention's own stories can be tested against doubles.  From the vision side, two carry-overs deserve priority even though they are not blockers, because both erode the core restraint fantasy: 1. E-38 and E-65 still call 'air and heat' a cost of restraint, which directly contradicts the guard rail at L121. 2. The Aud
Prior verdict resolved: Yes (confirming review of 2026-10-27)
Findings:
  - [RECOMMENDED] Edge Cases E-38 / E-65 vs Player Fantasy guard rail (L121): [main review, creative-director confirmed] L121 says going dark 'does **not** cost air or heat'. L1036 says 'the cost of restraint is time, air and heat' and L1043 says the same. This is the most tone-critical carry-over. Pillar 3 restraint has to read as a tactical trade (verbs, time, the inrush) and not as a resource tax. If restraint is a tax, players learn to stay lit, and the horror loop inverts.
  - [RECOMMENDED] Visual/Audio AUD-6 / M7 / AC-AT-78 vs adaptive-audio-and-tells.md: [main review, creative-director confirmed] adaptive-audio-and-tells.md has no 'void' cue. Its only match is the word 'avoid' at L1790. Every ABORTED outcome plays the restraint exhale, so a player who fled is told 'your restraint worked'. That is ludonarrative dissonance on the game's core verb. AC-AT-78's token check fails today.
  - [RECOMMENDED] player-controller-input.md BURDEN push / C33 / OQ-AT-37(1): [main review, creative-director confirmed] player-controller-input.md has 0 hits for BURDEN, although the registry names the Controller as the pusher. A story written from the Controller GDD would leave out the user-ruled carry burden and the item-keyed rearm cancel. This is not blocking for Attention, which can be tested against a double.
  - [RECOMMENDED] C35 / OQ-AT-29 / AC-AT-130 / AT-1, AT-8, AT-27: [main review] The restore_epoch gate still reads 'CONFLICT, not READY', although the kernel (request_restore, KRN-EPO-01..05) and Save/Load (SL-23, AC-SL-142/145) now carry the contract. This wrongly blocks stories that are ready.
  - [RECOMMENDED] Tuning Knobs TELL_DRAW_LO: [main review] The printed safe range starts at 780. The ring-1 home-lit lint row binds at 876, so values from 780 to 875 pass the printed range and fail AC-AT-64.
  - [RECOMMENDED] Cross-References table / Dependencies status cells / AC-AT-77, AC-AT-78: [main review] Seven neighbours are missing from 'This Document References'. About 30 status cells are stale ('In Design', 'undesigned', 'in flight') for GDDs that are now Designed.
  - [RECOMMENDED] horror-entities.md HE-F16 E_s: [main review] E_s is still marked provisional, although BREACHES_PER_SESSION 3-8 is registered and owned by Attention.
  - [RECOMMENDED] OQ-AT-38 / Last Verified / CD-GDD-ALIGN: [main review, creative-director concurs] The last CD-GDD-ALIGN pass was 2026-10-26, and a large set of rulings has landed since then. The 553 KB document interleaves provenance with rule text, and that hurts implementer readability. This is a vision-coherence risk, not a design defect.
  - [RECOMMENDED] AC-AT-134: [main review] 'Expected 0 by AT-10' is imprecise, because AT-10 allows a round-trip cancel when d > 1,290.

14	
15	## Summary
16	
17	The Attention System is the simulation of the web's regard for the ship: one global, integer-only level that rises with the light the crew burns, the noise they make, the power they draw and the depth they work at, and falls back toward a depth-set baseline when they show restraint. Crossing one threshold starts a seeded, escalating 15 to 30 second **tell** (sound in a structure-borne bed, filaments resolving at the lamp cone's edge, never a meter) that restraint can abort; if it is not aborted, a **breach** puts STRESS on the section where the crew was loudest and on everything welded to it, sweeps the home-ship's single beacon, and ends in a short silence. It owns the tell-window contract: no web-originated harm lands outside a told breach, which is how Pillars 2 and 3 become testable.
18	
19	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer (designed), Life-Support Graph (designed), Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query (designed), Player Controller & Input (designed), Save/Load & Versioned Format (designed), Suit & Equipment (designed; soft, none at MVP)`; neighbours designed after this GDD (rows refreshed in the 2026-10-27 consistency pass where asked): `Ship Body & Interior Physics, Web Map & Transit, Horror Entities, Sanity & Hallucination Rules, Adaptive Audio & Tells (Designed, adaptive-audio-and-tells.md)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Modular Ship Assembly, Perception Filter, Boarding & Salvage, HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments, Chart Table, Debug Overlay and Derelict Authoring are Designed too; a matching status does not mean matching contracts, see OQ-AT-28 for the contract-diff outcome)*
20	
21	## Overview
22	
23	The Attention System is the web's regard of the ship, as simulation. In one sentence: it is a scene-tree-free, integer-only `SIM` block, `attention.state`, advanced by one divisor-6 step hook, `attention.step`, that holds **one global attention level** which rises with the light the crew keeps burning, the noise they make, the power they draw and the depth they work at, falls back toward a depth-set baseline when they show restraint, and drives a four-phase breach machine, **CALM → TELL → BREACH → SUBSIDING**, whose second step, the tell, is a promise to the player: a window of 10 to 30 seconds, seeded and fixed at the moment the level crosses the threshold, in which the world escalates for as long as the crew stays loud and the player can still choose to be quiet *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
24	
25	**The data layer.** Stimuli reach the level by two paths and no others. *Pushed noise* arrives through one Class B mutator, `push_stimulus(kind, source_ref, class)`, from the Player Controller (gait classes, and one per-tick carry-burden class *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*), Interaction (tool and one-shot classes); Horror Entities never calls it (HE-36); Attention owns the unit table `U[class]`, and one walking tick of noise defines the unit (1 attention unit, AU). *Ordered reads* take light from the Emitter State's per-emitter list and power from the Life-Support Graph's `power_use(section_id)`; the Suit pushes nothing, and Attention never reads Audio. The level is held in milli-AU, integrates the three channels with one memory constant `TAU_ATT_TICKS`, and decays by a ceiling step toward the baseline `B`, so it always reaches `B` exactly. One threshold `ATT_THRESHOLD` (theta) with a hold band (theta_HOLD) starts and ends events. The machine's only writes to the world are two: M17 `deposit_trace(STRESS, ...)` at `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT`, and the `set_beacon` command. Everything else it does is **publish** `attention.view`, a SIM read view of integers that Lighting, Audio, Horror, Sanity, Save/Load and its own presenter read.
26	
27	**The player-facing effect.** The player never sees the level. They meet this system as the hull creaking, from everywhere and nowhere, and creaking again, a little sooner each time; as filaments at the very edge of their lamp's cone that were texture a moment ago and are now strands; as dust in the beam turning as if the air had been displaced. That is the **tell**, and its length is not shown. Inside it the player can do the one thing the web responds to, which is less: stand still and set the cutter and any cargo down (the real levers), and, helping a little, kill the chest lamp or open the breaker *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (the breaker saves about 2 seconds and its inrush on re-closing gives them back, so it is the least of these, F-25 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*). If the level falls under the hold band and stays there, the tell ends in nothing and the creaking stops (an abort). If it does not, the tell ends in a **breach**: the section where the crew was loudest, and every section welded to it, takes STRESS (worn hardware fails faster than a person can walk), the home-ship's single beacon sweeps red, and a short silence follows when it is over. The player can survive a breach, or leave it by pod; they cannot win it. Camera, controls, lamp and ambient light do not change in any phase.
28	
29	**The contract this GDD owns.** Every web-originated harm to the ship, and provisionally to a crew body, must land inside a told breach: a tell of at least `TELL_MIN_TICKS` (derived as `ticks_for_seconds(W_MIN_WARNING_S)`) that the player could perceive and could have aborted by restraint *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Audio is the guaranteed channel**: the structure-borne bed reaches every living player whatever is lit. The visual channel exists while an eligible emitter is lit, so a player who is fully dark has the audio channel only (ART:954 accepts this). The levers that abort a tell do not weigh the same: **stopping movement and stopping the tool are the lever; darkness and power-down help a little** (F-25 lists the seconds each saves). The Graph's fairness gate covers *endogenous* losses only (LS-13); for every non-player source it states "must therefore be preceded by that system's own Pillar 2 tell". This GDD is that tell. It is written as a testable predicate, `tell_window_contract`, audited by a `TellAudit` ledger that exists as a test fixture before Horror Entities and Adaptive Audio are designed, and it discharges the Graph's review criterion at LSG:1063.
30	
31	**What the game loses without it.** The core loop's hinge ("Light, noise, power spikes and depth raise it; it is shown in the world; crossing a line flips the rhythm. Dread is feeling it come." — game concept, Core Loop) would be a flat spawn timer, which is the exact outcome Pillar 3's design test rejects, or a hidden threshold, which Pillar 2's design test rejects. Horror Entities would have no phase to act inside and no permission predicate to honour; Save/Load would have no tell to defer an autosave around; Lighting would have no tier to gutter on; Adaptive Audio would have no beat to sound; Sanity would have no true, unhideable event to measure a lie against. The core hypothesis (the two-rhythm boarding-and-breach loop is tense and absorbing for a 30-minute solo session) cannot be tested without it.
32	
33	**MVP scope.** One threshold, one tier of lamp tell, one locus rule, one breach content (STRESS plus beacon plus published phase; RUPTURE and GOUGE are Horror's), one noise-only push API, ring-1 baseline plus placeholder rows for rings 2 and 3, and a contract-only suppressant (no effect verb, and the item itself is out of the MVP start kit, user ruling X6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Multiple tiers, per-ring thresholds, the suppressant verb, per-player attribution and rate-coupled tell length are Vertical Slice addenda and are named, not absorbed (AT-30); the per-ring light and power stimulus gain is a pillar-flagged Vertical Slice requirement on Depth Rings & Scarcity (AT-6); phantom tells and false calm are rejected by pillar, permanently (AT-17).
34	
35	**Index wording reconciled.** The index rationale (IDX Systems Enumeration bullet 17) is honoured with five corrections, each recorded as a refresh owed and never as an edit:
36	
37	| The index says | This GDD does | Why | Refresh owed |
38	|---|---|---|---|
39	| noise and power stimuli "pushed in by Graph, Suit, Interaction, Assembly and Horrors" | **two intake paths**: noise is pushed (Controller, Interaction; Horror pushes none and is not a declared caller, HE-36); light and power are *ordered reads* (`emitters()`, `power_use`); Suit and Assembly push nothing at MVP | the Graph publishes `power_use` as a read (LS-19); Suit declares "No stimuli pushed" (SE-31); Interaction already pushes LOUD at cut completion (IA-33), so an Assembly push would double count | index bullet 17 wording (C6); kernel Interactions row 4 (C7) |
40	| "flicker as a Lighting modifier" | the lamp effect is a **gutter**, published as a tier | Lighting bans the word for the tell (LO-19, LO-20) | index wording (C10) |
41	| "Lighting never reads Attention" (IDX soft-cycle note) | Lighting reads only the published tier and timing; Attention reads nothing Lighting produces | LO-20 supersedes it | index soft-cycle note (C12) |
42	| "baseline set by depth" | `B = B_table[ring]` of the deepest section holding a living player; per-ring values belong to Depth Rings (VS) | one deterministic rule; "loudest player" is undefined | none |
43	| Suit listed as a Hard dependency | Suit is **soft, none at MVP**: contract text for the suppressant only | Suit pushes nothing and Attention reads nothing of it | index edge Attention → Suit (C14) |
44	
45	**Reading guide.** Detailed Design holds the thirty-odd named rules `AT-1` to `AT-32` (Core Rules), the state machine, and one Interactions table per neighbour. Numbers in this document are `[PLACEHOLDER]` unless a registry name says otherwise; every locked constant (`TICK_RATE`, `W_MIN_WARNING_S`, `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT`, `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS`, `NOISE_PER_TICK`, `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`, `MAX_EMITTERS`, `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`, `AUTOSAVE_*`, `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS`, `MOD_FLOOR_PM`) is cited by name and never restated with a number of this document's own. Lighting's **`gutter_recipe` bounds** (its variables `G_LO` and `G_HI`, tier 1 at 480 and 960 frames, REG:2187-2188, registry `gutter_recipe` variables) are not registry entries: they are cited as "Lighting's `gutter_recipe` bounds" and take no `referenced_by` from this document (C24).
46	
47	**Implementation digest** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(one page for story authors; the rule ids carry the detail and where this digest and a rule differ, the rule wins).* (1) *Shape:* one `SIM` block `attention.state` (WORLD, SHARED, schema 1) and one hook `attention.step` at divisor 6, offset 0, `after [graph.propagate.power, emitter.place]`; integer-only; the only `rng_derive` is the tell draw (AT-1, AT-28). (2) *Intake:* noise by `push_stimulus(NOISE, source, class)` from the Controller and Interaction only (the Controller also pushes one per-tick carry-burden class, F-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, attributed to a section at push time into `pending_noise_mAU` and `pending_ledger_mAU[s]`; light from `emitters()`; power from `power_use` as `W_P × nl_w` plus `W_S ×` a lamp-excluded five-run delta from Attention's own `nl_hist_w` (AT-3, AT-4, F-1 to F-4). (3) *Level:* `L' = clamp(L + I_run − dec, B, L_CEIL)` with `dec = ceil(6 (L − B) / tau)`, and `dec = 0` on a run that drained a `BURDEN` push (a salvage carry held aboard a non-home body, not `IN_POD`, AT-3) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*; `B` from the deepest living seat's ring (AT-5, AT-6, F-5, F-8). (4) *Machine:* CALM to TELL (at `L ≥ theta`, past both timers), TELL to BREACH (due run, `L ≥ theta_HOLD`, not `locus_vacated`), BREACH to SUBSIDING to CALM; TELL to CALM on an abort (twenty runs under the hold line, or at the due run under it, or the departure void) (AT-7 to AT-13, AT-22). (5) *Tell:* length drawn once (900 to 1800 ticks, floor 600 on every path) under a key that changes per restore epoch; beats on a hash schedule whose interval and tier follow a behaviour-keyed escalation clock (frozen while `L < theta_HOLD`) with one counter for both senses; nothing published reveals the end (AT-8, AT-9, AT-16) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (6) *Breach:* STRESS on the locus body in bursts, `set_beacon` at T+1; light and power feed the locus ledger through their own sections and noise dominates it (AT-11, AT-12, AT-14, AT-18, F-6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. (7) *Contract:* `exogenous_permitted(section)` and the `TellAudit` replay are the testable form of Pillars 2 and 3 (AT-15, F-23). (8) *Persisted:* the field list in AT-1; every restore failure is a hard `ATTENTION_RESTORE_*` and nothing is clamped. (9) *Lints that gate data:* F-15 and F-15b abortability (rows `x_dark`, `x_dark_home_lit`, `autonomous_transient`), F-16 dark floor, F-20 and F-21 autosave deferral, IR-1 to IR-3, IR-4 (`carry_decision`, F-26), the DOCK_STATUS budget (F-16), F-24 cue floor and rung width, the theta upper bound (F-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (10) *Not built here:* Horror's behaviours, Audio's sounds, Lighting's gutter, the suppressant verb, the per-ring gain (AT-30). **Provenance codes (key).** `Rn` and `CQ-n` are rulings and checkpoint questions of the 2026-10-26 authoring run, `CP-Cn` and `GD-n` are consistency-pass and game-designer findings, `Cn` rows are refreshes owed (Cross-References), `AF-n` are art flags and `Xn` are additions. The ruling files are not in the repository, so the rule text is authoritative and a code is only a pointer; moving rationale into a separate decision log is recorded in OQ-AT-28 and not done in this pass.
48

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

</system-reminder>

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

14	
15	## Summary
16	
17	The Attention System is the simulation of the web's regard for the ship: one global, integer-only level that rises with the light the crew burns, the noise they make, the power they draw and the depth they work at, and falls back toward a depth-set baseline when they show restraint. Crossing one threshold starts a seeded, escalating 15 to 30 second **tell** (sound in a structure-borne bed, filaments resolving at the lamp cone's edge, never a meter) that restraint can abort; if it is not aborted, a **breach** puts STRESS on the section where the crew was loudest and on everything welded to it, sweeps the home-ship's single beacon, and ends in a short silence. It owns the tell-window contract: no web-originated harm lands outside a told breach, which is how Pillars 2 and 3 become testable.
18	
19	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer (designed), Life-Support Graph (designed), Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query (designed), Player Controller & Input (designed), Save/Load & Versioned Format (designed), Suit & Equipment (designed; soft, none at MVP)`; neighbours designed after this GDD (rows refreshed in the 2026-10-27 consistency pass where asked): `Ship Body & Interior Physics, Web Map & Transit, Horror Entities, Sanity & Hallucination Rules, Adaptive Audio & Tells (Designed, adaptive-audio-and-tells.md)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Modular Ship Assembly, Perception Filter, Boarding & Salvage, HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments, Chart Table, Debug Overlay and Derelict Authoring are Designed too; a matching status does not mean matching contracts, see OQ-AT-28 for the contract-diff outcome)*
20	
21	## Overview
22	
23	The Attention System is the web's regard of the ship, as simulation. In one sentence: it is a scene-tree-free, integer-only `SIM` block, `attention.state`, advanced by one divisor-6 step hook, `attention.step`, that holds **one global attention level** which rises with the light the crew keeps burning, the noise they make, the power they draw and the depth they work at, falls back toward a depth-set baseline when they show restraint, and drives a four-phase breach machine, **CALM → TELL → BREACH → SUBSIDING**, whose second step, the tell, is a promise to the player: a window of 10 to 30 seconds, seeded and fixed at the moment the level crosses the threshold, in which the world escalates for as long as the crew stays loud and the player can still choose to be quiet *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
24	
25	**The data layer.** Stimuli reach the level by two paths and no others. *Pushed noise* arrives through one Class B mutator, `push_stimulus(kind, source_ref, class)`, from the Player Controller (gait classes, and one per-tick carry-burden class *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*), Interaction (tool and one-shot classes); Horror Entities never calls it (HE-36); Attention owns the unit table `U[class]`, and one walking tick of noise defines the unit (1 attention unit, AU). *Ordered reads* take light from the Emitter State's per-emitter list and power from the Life-Support Graph's `power_use(section_id)`; the Suit pushes nothing, and Attention never reads Audio. The level is held in milli-AU, integrates the three channels with one memory constant `TAU_ATT_TICKS`, and decays by a ceiling step toward the baseline `B`, so it always reaches `B` exactly. One threshold `ATT_THRESHOLD` (theta) with a hold band (theta_HOLD) starts and ends events. The machine's only writes to the world are two: M17 `deposit_trace(STRESS, ...)` at `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT`, and the `set_beacon` command. Everything else it does is **publish** `attention.view`, a SIM read view of integers that Lighting, Audio, Horror, Sanity, Save/Load and its own presenter read.
26	
27	**The player-facing effect.** The player never sees the level. They meet this system as the hull creaking, from everywhere and nowhere, and creaking again, a little sooner each time; as filaments at the very edge of their lamp's cone that were texture a moment ago and are now strands; as dust in the beam turning as if the air had been displaced. That is the **tell**, and its length is not shown. Inside it the player can do the one thing the web responds to, which is less: stand still and set the cutter and any cargo down (the real levers), and, helping a little, kill the chest lamp or open the breaker *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (the breaker saves about 2 seconds and its inrush on re-closing gives them back, so it is the least of these, F-25 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*). If the level falls under the hold band and stays there, the tell ends in nothing and the creaking stops (an abort). If it does not, the tell ends in a **breach**: the section where the crew was loudest, and every section welded to it, takes STRESS (worn hardware fails faster than a person can walk), the home-ship's single beacon sweeps red, and a short silence follows when it is over. The player can survive a breach, or leave it by pod; they cannot win it. Camera, controls, lamp and ambient light do not change in any phase.
28	
29	**The contract this GDD owns.** Every web-originated harm to the ship, and provisionally to a crew body, must land inside a told breach: a tell of at least `TELL_MIN_TICKS` (derived as `ticks_for_seconds(W_MIN_WARNING_S)`) that the player could perceive and could have aborted by restraint *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Audio is the guaranteed channel**: the structure-borne bed reaches every living player whatever is lit. The visual channel exists while an eligible emitter is lit, so a player who is fully dark has the audio channel only (ART:954 accepts this). The levers that abort a tell do not weigh the same: **stopping movement and stopping the tool are the lever; darkness and power-down help a little** (F-25 lists the seconds each saves). The Graph's fairness gate covers *endogenous* losses only (LS-13); for every non-player source it states "must therefore be preceded by that system's own Pillar 2 tell". This GDD is that tell. It is written as a testable predicate, `tell_window_contract`, audited by a `TellAudit` ledger that exists as a test fixture before Horror Entities and Adaptive Audio are designed, and it discharges the Graph's review criterion at LSG:1063.
30	
31	**What the game loses without it.** The core loop's hinge ("Light, noise, power spikes and depth raise it; it is shown in the world; crossing a line flips the rhythm. Dread is feeling it come." — game concept, Core Loop) would be a flat spawn timer, which is the exact outcome Pillar 3's design test rejects, or a hidden threshold, which Pillar 2's design test rejects. Horror Entities would have no phase to act inside and no permission predicate to honour; Save/Load would have no tell to defer an autosave around; Lighting would have no tier to gutter on; Adaptive Audio would have no beat to sound; Sanity would have no true, unhideable event to measure a lie against. The core hypothesis (the two-rhythm boarding-and-breach loop is tense and absorbing for a 30-minute solo session) cannot be tested without it.
32	
33	**MVP scope.** One threshold, one tier of lamp tell, one locus rule, one breach content (STRESS plus beacon plus published phase; RUPTURE and GOUGE are Horror's), one noise-only push API, ring-1 baseline plus placeholder rows for rings 2 and 3, and a contract-only suppressant (no effect verb, and the item itself is out of the MVP start kit, user ruling X6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Multiple tiers, per-ring thresholds, the suppressant verb, per-player attribution and rate-coupled tell length are Vertical Slice addenda and are named, not absorbed (AT-30); the per-ring light and power stimulus gain is a pillar-flagged Vertical Slice requirement on Depth Rings & Scarcity (AT-6); phantom tells and false calm are rejected by pillar, permanently (AT-17).
34	
35	**Index wording reconciled.** The index rationale (IDX Systems Enumeration bullet 17) is honoured with five corrections, each recorded as a refresh owed and never as an edit:
36	
37	| The index says | This GDD does | Why | Refresh owed |
38	|---|---|---|---|
39	| noise and power stimuli "pushed in by Graph, Suit, Interaction, Assembly and Horrors" | **two intake paths**: noise is pushed (Controller, Interaction; Horror pushes none and is not a declared caller, HE-36); light and power are *ordered reads* (`emitters()`, `power_use`); Suit and Assembly push nothing at MVP | the Graph publishes `power_use` as a read (LS-19); Suit declares "No stimuli pushed" (SE-31); Interaction already pushes LOUD at cut completion (IA-33), so an Assembly push would double count | index bullet 17 wording (C6); kernel Interactions row 4 (C7) |
40	| "flicker as a Lighting modifier" | the lamp effect is a **gutter**, published as a tier | Lighting bans the word for the tell (LO-19, LO-20) | index wording (C10) |
41	| "Lighting never reads Attention" (IDX soft-cycle note) | Lighting reads only the published tier and timing; Attention reads nothing Lighting produces | LO-20 supersedes it | index soft-cycle note (C12) |
42	| "baseline set by depth" | `B = B_table[ring]` of the deepest section holding a living player; per-ring values belong to Depth Rings (VS) | one deterministic rule; "loudest player" is undefined | none |
43	| Suit listed as a Hard dependency | Suit is **soft, none at MVP**: contract text for the suppressant only | Suit pushes nothing and Attention reads nothing of it | index edge Attention → Suit (C14) |
44	
45	**Reading guide.** Detailed Design holds the thirty-odd named rules `AT-1` to `AT-32` (Core Rules), the state machine, and one Interactions table per neighbour. Numbers in this document are `[PLACEHOLDER]` unless a registry name says otherwise; every locked constant (`TICK_RATE`, `W_MIN_WARNING_S`, `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT`, `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS`, `NOISE_PER_TICK`, `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`, `MAX_EMITTERS`, `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`, `AUTOSAVE_*`, `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS`, `MOD_FLOOR_PM`) is cited by name and never restated with a number of this document's own. Lighting's **`gutter_recipe` bounds** (its variables `G_LO` and `G_HI`, tier 1 at 480 and 960 frames, REG:2187-2188, registry `gutter_recipe` variables) are not registry entries: they are cited as "Lighting's `gutter_recipe` bounds" and take no `referenced_by` from this document (C24).
46	
47	**Implementation digest** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(one page for story authors; the rule ids carry the detail and where this digest and a rule differ, the rule wins).* (1) *Shape:* one `SIM` block `attention.state` (WORLD, SHARED, schema 1) and one hook `attention.step` at divisor 6, offset 0, `after [graph.propagate.power, emitter.place]`; integer-only; the only `rng_derive` is the tell draw (AT-1, AT-28). (2) *Intake:* noise by `push_stimulus(NOISE, source, class)` from the Controller and Interaction only (the Controller also pushes one per-tick carry-burden class, F-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, attributed to a section at push time into `pending_noise_mAU` and `pending_ledger_mAU[s]`; light from `emitters()`; power from `power_use` as `W_P × nl_w` plus `W_S ×` a lamp-excluded five-run delta from Attention's own `nl_hist_w` (AT-3, AT-4, F-1 to F-4). (3) *Level:* `L' = clamp(L + I_run − dec, B, L_CEIL)` with `dec = ceil(6 (L − B) / tau)`, and `dec = 0` on a run that drained a `BURDEN` push (a salvage carry held aboard a non-home body, not `IN_POD`, AT-3) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*; `B` from the deepest living seat's ring (AT-5, AT-6, F-5, F-8). (4) *Machine:* CALM to TELL (at `L ≥ theta`, past both timers), TELL to BREACH (due run, `L ≥ theta_HOLD`, not `locus_vacated`), BREACH to SUBSIDING to CALM; TELL to CALM on an abort (twenty runs under the hold line, or at the due run under it, or the departure void) (AT-7 to AT-13, AT-22). (5) *Tell:* length drawn once (900 to 1800 ticks, floor 600 on every path) under a key that changes per restore epoch; beats on a hash schedule whose interval and tier follow a behaviour-keyed escalation clock (frozen while `L < theta_HOLD`) with one counter for both senses; nothing published reveals the end (AT-8, AT-9, AT-16) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (6) *Breach:* STRESS on the locus body in bursts, `set_beacon` at T+1; light and power feed the locus ledger through their own sections and noise dominates it (AT-11, AT-12, AT-14, AT-18, F-6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. (7) *Contract:* `exogenous_permitted(section)` and the `TellAudit` replay are the testable form of Pillars 2 and 3 (AT-15, F-23). (8) *Persisted:* the field list in AT-1; every restore failure is a hard `ATTENTION_RESTORE_*` and nothing is clamped. (9) *Lints that gate data:* F-15 and F-15b abortability (rows `x_dark`, `x_dark_home_lit`, `autonomous_transient`), F-16 dark floor, F-20 and F-21 autosave deferral, IR-1 to IR-3, IR-4 (`carry_decision`, F-26), the DOCK_STATUS budget (F-16), F-24 cue floor and rung width, the theta upper bound (F-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (10) *Not built here:* Horror's behaviours, Audio's sounds, Lighting's gutter, the suppressant verb, the per-ring gain (AT-30). **Provenance codes (key).** `Rn` and `CQ-n` are rulings and checkpoint questions of the 2026-10-26 authoring run, `CP-Cn` and `GD-n` are consistency-pass and game-designer findings, `Cn` rows are refreshes owed (Cross-References), `AF-n` are art flags and `Xn` are additions. The ruling files are not in the repository, so the rule text is authoritative and a code is only a pointer; moving rationale into a separate decision log is recorded in OQ-AT-28 and not done in this pass.

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.

The magnitude is cited by registry name and never as a number; passing that constant as `magnitude` also makes the Graph's M17 clamp reading (`stress_pm = clamp(magnitude, 1000, 3000)`) and its D.9 / LS-25 reading (`stress_pm = BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT`) agree (C15, a Graph wording refresh). **Footprint cap:** `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` bounds honoured footprints per Graph run; Attention takes at most `STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` per run. **Attention has no first claim on the cap** (CP-C5): Horror's footprints arrive by **path (a)**: the published Class B mutators `deposit_trace` (M17) and `apply_suit_damage`, called from the `horror.step` hook, which is ordered `after` Attention (KRN Interactions row 9; Horror HE-28, C-HE-3), not as SYSTEM commands in P2; Horror submits no SYSTEM command at MVP. The Graph's "first `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` in arrival order within P2" (LSG:807) carries a P2 premise that path (a) does not satisfy, so Attention claims no first place in the cap. The guarantee is therefore a **Horror must-repeat**: its per-run footprint budget is at most `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP − STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN`. The registry unit of `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` (revised 2026-10-27) says per run across all callers and subjects (global), the first 16 by arrival applied in ascending subject id and the rest dropped and counted, which matches LSG:727 (C22). A STRESS deposit the cap drops is not lost for good: the next burst run re-arms it (AT-12; an edge case below). **Attention's MVP breach is STRESS plus the beacon plus the published phase.** RUPTURE and GOUGE are Horror's; this keeps Attention fully testable without Horror. **Stance (the breach is a consequence amplifier, stated so it is a decision):** STRESS multiplies *endogenous* damage only ("the breach rhythm makes the ship *fail* faster, not *leak* faster", LSG D.9), so a breach costs the crew what they had deferred; on a clean ship it would be nearly a non-event. **Why this is not left as a stance (gate ruling, CD-GDD-ALIGN, applied):** each choice is defensible alone, but a toothless breach on a clean ship together with an abort that always forfeits the partial (AT-10, Moment A) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* makes *commit* the dominant choice. Restraint would always cost the partial, riding it out would cost almost nothing, P3's "restraint and stealth are real strategies" would be empty, the "chaos" half of P2 would have no chaos, and players would learn to ignore tells. Two requirements follow, and neither is a mitigation to be traded away. **(1) Content requirement (a Derelict Authoring must-repeat).** Every body that can be a locus on MVP derelicts A and B is authored with at least one active overload or fatigue fault (on derelict A, a fault that wakes when its bus is served: option (b), OQ-AT-24), so a derelict breach always has something to amplify (AC-AT-58 is the seeded-fault scenario, AC-AT-117 the authoring check). This fits P5: the outer ring is kept unsafe by wear. A body the player has repaired clean is the player's earned result and not a content failure, and a home-ship locus carries whatever the crew has left unrepaired. **(2) Horror Entities' single MVP behaviour wired to BREACH is a BLOCKING dependency** (OQ-AT-9, AC-AT-77), no longer an ask: a breach brings the thing the crew fears, not only a faster-failing hull. `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT` is not raised to hide this. **Playtest tripwire:** the Moment-ordering guard (Player Fantasy, AC-AT-80) is named for exactly this failure: a 30-minute session with only breaches means commit has become dominant. **Re-evaluated against the designed Horror and Derelict Authoring** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the claim that STRESS alone leaves a derelict breach toothless was written before Horror existed. Horror now supplies crew-side teeth of its own: by HE-F16 a stationary seat in the locus body cannot be killed in a minimum-length breach (`BREACH_MIN_TICKS` 900 gives two REACH starts) but can be in any breach of at least 986 ticks and certainly in any of at least 1,156, and the REACH ladder (HE-F13, HE-F17) gives the breach a content beat. The breach therefore has two teeth: STRESS (ship-side, it amplifies deferred faults) and Horror's REACH (crew-side, it needs a seat that lingers); neither substitutes for the other, and a crew that leaves the body by pod is exposed to neither beyond the STRESS tail. Requirement (1) stays as the ship-side tooth. **Derelict A, option (b)** (creative-director recommendation; **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), OQ-AT-24: option (b)**, which preserves EM-24's count of 8 live faults; the dead-bus exemption (a) is not adopted) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: its pass condition is a Graph subject authored with a fault that *wakes when its bus is served* (`j_a_main`, a dead SHORT that becomes live once fed, with `pump_a` on its branch), which keeps Emitter State's count of exactly 8 live faults (EM-24) and adds no ninth fault. **Story-readiness gate:** a story that builds AT-11, the breach ACs or Derelict Authoring's locus lint is not ready until AC-AT-58's tolerance is fixed with the Graph owner (OQ-AT-6); OQ-AT-24 is answered (user ruling, option (b)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
208	*Criterion.* AC-AT-28, AC-AT-29, AC-AT-30, AC-AT-58 (seeded-fault scenario). *Pillar.* P2, P3. *Decided by:* R12; LSG:196, :525, :906.
209	
210	**AT-12. Breach duration and end.** *Rule.* During BREACH the level **keeps integrating** (the player's noise still matters), with `W_L[FAULT_GLOW] = W_L[BEACON] = 0` and the beacon's lamp watts never reaching the power terms (`bcn_main` is a LAMP node, so it sits inside `lamps_lit_w`, AT-4; the alarm cannot hold the level above `theta_HOLD` and delay the exit it is tested against) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. STRESS is re-armed in **bursts**: `STRESS_REFRESH_BURST_RUNS` (3) consecutive runs every `STRESS_REFRESH_RUNS` (placeholder 300) runs, under the lint `STRESS_REFRESH_RUNS + STRESS_REFRESH_BURST_RUNS < STRESS_HOLD_STEPS` (cited from LSG:907; registry `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS`). A burst tolerates one dropped deposit because a deposit is idempotent. BREACH ends at the first of: (i) `BREACH_MAX_TICKS` (placeholder 3600, the death-spiral guard); (ii) after `BREACH_MIN_TICKS` (placeholder 900), `L < theta_HOLD` for `CLEAR_HOLD_TICKS` (placeholder 300, run-quantised); (iii) pod-hop departure: the last living occupant recorded at BREACH entry (`locus_occupants_at_entry`) leaving a locus body that is not the home-ship (AT-22); (iv) **ADDITION X10 (APPROVED at the CD-GDD-ALIGN gate: the combat anti-pillar explicitly permits decoys, and the lit derelict pays in STRESS on its own hardware; CR-LURE stays a playtest watch item with `LOCUS_OCC_PREF_PM` as the lever):** if at BREACH entry the locus body is not the home-ship and `locus_occupants_at_entry` is empty (it holds no living player), at `BREACH_MIN_TICKS` (the retreat the departure clause models has already happened) (reachable at MVP only through a derelict that Web Map keeps loaded while berthed, WM-21 and WM-24, after the player has left it; a *departed* unberthed derelict goes dormant at once under LS-17's default, which Web Map adopts, so that form is fixture-only *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*). **Breach length is Attention's, not `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS`.** STRESS lapses on the Graph's own hold after the last deposit and may outlast SUBSIDING: "a long tell, a spreading wrongness, a short collapse, then silence" (LSG:986). No Attention surface shows that tail. **Must-repeat request to Adaptive Audio & Tells (R30):** `phase == CALM` is never mapped to an "all clear" cue, because the Graph's consequence sounds, not Attention, carry the ongoing wrongness; this is Audio's rule to repeat, not Attention's.
211	*Criterion.* AC-AT-31, AC-AT-32, AC-AT-33 (lint), AC-AT-34. *Pillar.* P2, P3. *Decided by:* R12.
212	
213	**AT-13. Subsiding and the refractory.** *Rule.* On SUBSIDING entry: `set_beacon(off)` is submitted; no further STRESS deposits are made; and the level is reset to a residual, not wiped: `L ← min(L, B + POST_PM × (theta − B) / 1000)` with `POST_PM` a placeholder of 400. SUBSIDING lasts `SUBSIDE_TICKS` (placeholder 1200) while integrating normally, then the machine returns to CALM with `refract_until_T = T + REFRACT_TICKS` (placeholder 1800) and `tell_outcome = BREACHED`. During the refractory no TELL may begin, but the level keeps integrating, so **the refractory is not free safe time**: a player still loud at its end tips straight into a new tell (bounded by `L_CEIL`). The refractory is a published, state-gated valley, not a hidden scheduler. `phase` changes only inside `attention.step`; `post_restore` changes no phase and submits nothing (AT-27), so no reader can observe a half state; CALM → BREACH, TELL → SUBSIDING and BREACH → TELL do not exist. The phase table, guards and who may cause each transition are in States and Transitions.
214	*Criterion.* AC-AT-35, AC-AT-36, AC-AT-60 (table-driven transition test). *Pillar.* P2. *Decided by:* R13; LSG:986.
215	
216	**AT-14. Locus and locus body.** *Rule.* The **locus** is the section with the highest `ledger_mAU` at TELL entry; ties go to the lowest `section_id`. It is fixed for the epoch and falls back to the home-ship's lowest `section_id` only if the locus section is cut away or goes dormant *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* and no departure void applies: the fallback never converts an escape into a breach on the ship the player escaped to (AT-22, E-23). **During a TELL the dormancy fallback is suppressed from the first run at which `locus_vacated` holds** (a non-home locus body, `tell_occupants_at_entry` non-empty, no living seat in `locus_body`): the departure apply makes the derelict dormant many runs before `breach_due_T`, and without this the fallback would re-point the locus at the home ship in between and the due-run void would then never see the recorded body. The locus stays pinned to the departed body for the epoch (`locus_section_id` and `locus_body` remain valid ids; its ledger entry is dropped per AT-2, which is harmless because the locus is fixed), and the void resolves at the due run. The fallback is taken during a TELL only for a cut, a berth release, or a dormancy with a living seat still in the body. Attribution: a PlayerId source maps to the section containing the actor's foot origin through Ship Body's `actor_section(actor_id)` (BDY-29, Section lookup for Suit; sibling in flight); an object or emitter source maps to `section_of` or the emitter's `section_id`; light and power map to their own section. The **locus body** is `sections_of(body_of(locus))` (Layout reads, LY state inventory and Body row), recorded at TELL entry as `locus_body`. STRESS covers the whole locus body: welded sections share the breach, so a welded derelict is not a safe harbour. An optional knob `LOCUS_OCC_PREF_PM` (default 1000 = "leader only", conforming) lets a tuner prefer a section holding a living player if playtests show an unattended, powered derelict absorbing most breaches. Layout's pathing asks (`room_surface`, `floor_tile_at`, `room_adjacency`, LY Interactions row for Attention / Horror) are Horror's; Attention takes only the membership reads.
217	*Criterion.* AC-AT-37, AC-AT-59 (decoy knob default reproduces the rule). *Pillar.* P3. *Decided by:* R14.
218	
219	#### Group F — The contract, the view, the truth channel
220	
221	**AT-15. The tell-window contract: one predicate for all web-originated harm.** *Rule.* `exogenous_permitted(section) = phase ∈ {BREACH, SUBSIDING} AND section ∈ locus_body`. Every web-originated exogenous call (M17 RUPTURE, GOUGE and STRESS; environmental M18 `apply_damage(..., EXOGENOUS)`) must satisfy it. A `TellAudit` ledger (a DIAGNOSTIC subscriber and a **test fixture first**, written before Horror and Audio exist) records each such call as `(tick, caller, kind, section, tell_epoch, phase)`; it also records every AT-14 fallback as `LOCUS_FALLBACK(epoch, old_body, new_body, tick)`, and the replay evaluates `section_e` against the body in force at `t_e`; the replay asserts, for every harm event `e`, that some epoch `k` satisfies `tell_start_k + tell_len_k ≤ t_e < subside_end_k` with `tell_len_k ≥ TELL_MIN_TICKS` and `section_e ∈ locus_body_k` (registry formula `tell_window_contract`). **Scope (R15, provisional):** TellAudit also records every lethal act by a horror on a crew body, because the Pillar 2 promise ("every breach is preceded by a 10–30 second tell") is a promise to the *player*, not to the hull; a lethal act outside a told breach is exactly the ambush Pillar 2 forbids, and Horror's stalk is additive, never a substitute. **Horror Entities must REPEAT this rule or surface a CONFLICT.** "Perceivable" is defined relative to **every living player**, not to the locus: the tell must be audible to all of them through the non-positional structure-borne bed, whose existence and listener scope are contractual (its dB margin is Audio's). The bed is what makes a tell on an unoccupied lit derelict fair. Player-originated exogenous acts (cut, vent) never need the tell (LSG:144: agency); the Graph's endogenous gate (`W_MIN_WARNING_S`) is not how this contract is enforced and neither replaces nor is replaced by it. **This rule discharges LSG:1063** ("every call site of M17 RUPTURE, GOUGE and STRESS and every environmental M18 `apply_damage(…, EXOGENOUS)` source is preceded by that system's own 10–30 s Pillar 2 tell, named in its GDD, and none relies on the Graph's gate for it").
222	*Criterion.* AC-AT-01 (first; discharges LSG:1063), AC-AT-01a, AC-AT-68 (the provisional crew-body scope). *Pillar.* P2. *Decided by:* R15; LSG:144, :1063.
