**WM-26 — Hops and Attention.** *Rule.* The hop is **always allowed** during a TELL or BREACH (it is the escape verb, AT:73); this system pushes **no stimulus** (it makes 0 `push_stimulus` calls; the berth's single declared LOUD report is Interaction's, see "The berth is not silent to the Web" below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G1)*; the pod's running light is cosmetic presentation, not an eligible emitter (ASK-A1, accepted: AT-22 and AT V13 hold `held_ring` 1 for a hop between two ring-1 loci and count the pod's lights only if authored as an eligible FIXTURE, which they are not). Departure does not abort a TELL (AT-22): the clock, the bed and the beats run through the hop, and `tell_epoch`, `tell_len` and `breach_due_T` are unchanged. **The departure void (Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling, design-review decisions, Attention OQ-AT-12; Attention AT-22 and E-23 state it):** if the locus body is not the home-ship body and every seat recorded in it at TELL entry has left it by the due run (Attention's `locus_vacated`, derivable from Body's `body_of_actor` / `actor_section` and the IN_POD state of the Controller), the due run is an ABORT: TELL to CALM, `tell_outcome` ABORTED, no STRESS on any body, no beacon, `rearm_until_T` set, release cue. A home-ship locus is not voidable: there is no escape by pod from a breach centred on the home ship (Moment B variant). **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), OQ-AT-12 (2):** a home-ship-locus tell is NOT escapable by hopping to a derelict; 'the lights you left on' is the price *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **Reply to Web Map ASK-A4 (WM-26b, OQ-WM-42): declined** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: Attention does not hold the TELL-to-STRESS transfer while no seat is aboard the home body; a home-ship-locus breach proceeds as ruled, because holding it until someone returns would turn the hop into a way to defer a home breach, which the ruling above forbids. Web Map closed ASK-A4 as DECLINED and withdrew ASK-G5 on 2026-10-28 (WM-26b, delegated ruling R21) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. With the void, a hop away from a non-home locus never moves STRESS onto the home ship, so WM-26's former sentence 'the due-run breach STRESSes the home ship' described behaviour this document no longer has, and Web Map removed it on 2026-10-28; the home-ship locus with nobody aboard is E-73. A locus body that held no living seat at TELL entry (a lit, unoccupied, berthed derelict, WM-21) has nothing to void and breaches as before, ending under X10. BREACH ends when the last living occupant recorded at BREACH entry (`locus_occupants_at_entry`) leaves a locus body that is not the home-ship; a player who was never inside does not trigger it, and while any recorded occupant is still inside the clause is false. **Departure is derivable now** from Ship Body's `actor_section(actor_id)`: `locus_occupants_at_entry` is non-empty and no living seat's `actor_section` is in the recorded `locus_body` (a set of section ids), equivalently `body_of_actor(actor_id) ≠ body_of(locus_section_id)` for every living seat, plus the persisted `occ_gone` bits for recorded seats that are dead or cannot be resolved (F-14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, which makes the rule testable before Web Map exists; Web Map's pod-hop notification is `POD_DEPARTED` (WM-31 event table: `tick, leg_epoch, from, to, t0, n`; name confirmed; Save/Load also consumes one, SL event triggers) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. If the locus section is cut away or goes dormant mid-event, the locus falls back per AT-14 and the locus body is recomputed (never as the consequence of a departure, which the void above resolves first); STRESS already armed on a cut-away section lapses on its own hold. **A death in the pod** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(user ruling D60, 2026-10-27)*: statuses run in the pod (Suit's air, cell, thermal and counters, and the Sanity and Attention clocks, all keep running) and a seat that dies there is the Controller's `DEAD`; Attention reads that through `loco_state` (AT-31), so a seat in the pod is living until then, a dead one stops counting for `B` and for the pod hold, and if it was the last recorded occupant of a non-home locus its section had already left `locus_body`, so the departure clauses already hold. **Ordering in BREACH:** the departure test above is evaluated against the recorded `locus_body` before any dormancy fallback in the same run, so a pod departure that empties a non-home locus ends the breach and no fallback occurs (WM:87, Moment 2; E-27).

267	**AT-23. Co-op seams.** *Rule.* The `source` PlayerId tag is kept; one machine on one host; `repl_hint SHARED_SUMMARY`. Whether a downed crewmate's beam or a corpse is a lantern is noted only (EM open question). 270	**AT-24. Accessibility seams.** *Rule.* Reduce-motion: filament motion becomes a density change. Reduce-flashing: the gutter keeps its spacing (it passes by construction) and the beacon becomes a static mark (LO-26); reduce flashing defaults ON at first launch (user ruling D79), so the beacon is the static mark until the player turns it off *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. LO-26 also names a HUD glyph, which contradicts ART:741 and is routed as C27, so the static mark and the audio carry the breach; no glyph is drawn. **No captions are published for tell beats and no caption field exists**: a caption is an Attention indicator in effect (ART:741, :954); the generic "[creaking]" caption was weighed and not chosen, and no caption data is designed. **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), OQ-AT-1:** the deaf or muted player in the dark gets an **opt-in haptic pulse on beats**, off by default, because it carries the same information as the audio beat and so is not an indicator *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Contract: a PRESENTATION subscriber fires exactly one pulse per `(tell_epoch, tell_beat)` change, on the same notification as the audio request (so audio-first holds, AUD-2), at one fixed amplitude and duration; the pulse is never keyed to `level_pm`, `tier`, the cue step, the phase or anything but the beat; there is no pulse in CALM, none for pre-tell creaks, none for the alarm and none for the abort release. It is a setting under Display & Comfort (default off) whose wording says it repeats the beat and is not a meter, and it needs ART:741 and Adaptive Audio's AA-42 to admit it (a request to both; haptics driven only by the player's own true body cues, the Suit's, are not Attention indicators under the standing user decision, and Audio records that). With nothing lit there is still no visual channel (ART:954 accepts this); the audio channel is sufficient alone, for a deaf player with any eligible emitter lit (the beam, a fixture, a lantern or a glowstick) the visual channel is sufficient alone, and for a deaf or muted player in the dark the opt-in pulse is the channel. `design/accessibility-requirements.md` does not exist yet and is to be authored later with `/ux-design` accessibility; this paragraph is the Attention input to it.

273	**AT-25. One-way edges and the only writes.** *Rule.* Attention **reads only**: the Emitter State (`emitters()`), the Graph (`power_use`), Ship Body (`actor_section`, `body_of_actor`) and Layout (`body_of`, `sections_of`) lookups, the Controller's `loco_state` and `carry_ref` (AT-31; `carry_ref` for the item-keyed rearm only, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*) and Web Map's ring (provisional). It reads nothing from Lighting, Audio, Sanity, Horror, the Perception Filter, HUD, Instruments, Failure & Trail, Camera or Save/Load. It **writes the world only through two doors**: M17 STRESS and `set_beacon`. Lighting reads only the tier and timing (LO-20 supersedes the index's "Lighting never reads Attention", C12). There are lints in both directions: no Graph, Controller, Suit, Interaction-verb data, camera, Failure & Trail or Item DB code reads an Attention symbol (LSG:281, PCI:1010, SE-25, IA-4, PIPE:151, FT-4, IDB:473). 276	**AT-26. Pre-tell presentation in CALM is quantised and floor-gated.** *Rule.* `level_pm` may drive only **quantised, floor-gated, diegetic density**: ordinary hull-settling creaks and the count of cone-edge filaments, in `CUE_STEPS` (4) steps above `AMBIENT_CUE_FLOOR_PM` (800, **derived** by the calibration lint below and recorded in Tuning Knobs; the seed value 350 failed that lint, and the 2026-10-26 value 550 failed the recalibrated lint: it left step 1 on permanently during ordinary exploration with the home ship lit, C23) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, with a hysteresis `CUE_HYST_PM` (25) on the way down. **No continuous mapping of `level_pm` to any visible or audible parameter may exist**, because it would be an Attention meter by eye or by ear (ART:741, :64). **The ladder runs in CALM only** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: while `phase ≠ CALM` the step is forced to 0 and no pre-tell cue is requested, so a falling ladder can never become a live readout of abort progress during a TELL (guard rail 7; the creative-director accepted the semi-indicator for CALM only); after an abort or a SUBSIDING end the step re-arms from 0 and climbs again only across a rise edge, so pre-tell creaks never replay straight after the release cue (F-24). The computation is in Formulas (F-24): that state settles at `B + (1000 + 288 + 766 + 72) × TAU_ATT_TICKS` mAU, which is 4,127 AU at ring 1 (671 pm), 689 pm at ring 2 and 702 pm at ring 3, so the floor is the MVP-active ring's value plus `CUE_MARGIN_PM` (100), rounded up to the next 50: 800; the ring-3 test row would need 850 and is flagged `SWITCHES`. **Must-repeat request to Adaptive Audio & Tells (R30):** no music change precedes beat 0; adaptive music must not telegraph the tell earlier than the contract's start tick. 277	*Criterion.* AC-AT-49a to AC-AT-49c. *Pillar.* P3. *Decided by:* R27; Audio AA-22 (the pre-tell cue rule).

279	**AT-27. Persistence and restore.** *Rule.* `post_restore` rebuilds caches (section-id resolution, the sorted section arrays) and **nothing else**: it changes no `phase` and submits no command, because hooks receive `submit_system()` (KRN:593, :609) and a SYSTEM command pending at snapshot time is dropped on reload. The **beacon is reconciled in the first `attention.step` run after a restore**: the run compares `beacon_commanded` (persisted) with the emitter's switch state and submits `set_beacon` **only on a mismatch** (`phase == BREACH` and the beacon off: submit `on`; `phase != BREACH` and it on: submit `off`); no duplicate is submitted when the two already match, and a restore-time mismatch obeys the same `BEACON_RETRY_RUNS` retry as any rejection (AT-18). Cues fire on **transitions only**: loading a save made in any phase triggers no onset, no breach-enter and no release cue. The death stub restores from the newest verified autosave (SL-7) and Attention rolls back with it (WORLD scope); "Attention restores exactly; no meter is stored for display". A restore mid-TELL restores `rng_counter`, `tell_len`, `breach_due_T`, `tell_beat`, `esc_ticks`, `beat_next_off` and `below_hold_runs`, so no length is redrawn and the sequence is hash-identical; a draw made after a restore takes the new `restore_epoch` key (AT-8), so a death restore does not replay the next tell's length *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Restore coherence: `rng_counter ≤ tell_epoch` (an armed tell increments the epoch but not the counter); a block violating it fails with `ATTENTION_RESTORE_RNG_COUNTER` (AC-AT-70).

282	**AT-28. Determinism and RNG discipline.** *Rule.* Integer-only sim. The only `rng_derive` use is the tell draw (keyed per restore epoch, AT-8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Beat jitter and every presentation draw are pure integer hashes of `(tell_epoch, k, HASH_SEED)`; the hash is an ADR candidate shared with Lighting (LO-19). All sums are 64-bit and bounded; Attention uses sim `T` only, never wall time. A paused game stops `T` and so stops Attention.

Placeholders: 1800 + 3600 + 1200 + 300 = 6900, below the cited cap; the lint therefore binds `BREACH_MAX_TICKS` from above. Save/Load's ruled third soft-gate input (a bound seat at `vitals_state ≥ CRITICAL`, capped and then RISKY, user ruling D14) is a deferral cause that shares the same cap, so it adds no term and the inequality is unchanged (reading its cap as `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` is Save/Load's to confirm); the withheld Assembly-cut event autosave (D54) touches none of Attention's phases *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.

MVP scope.** *Rule.* MVP = one threshold, one tier of lamp tell, one locus rule, one breach content (STRESS plus beacon), one noise-only push API. **Vertical Slice addenda, not absorbed:** multiple tiers, per-ring thresholds, ring baselines beyond ring 1 and the per-ring stimulus gain (a pillar-flagged requirement, AT-6), the suppressant verb, per-player attribution, rate-coupled tell length, co-op scaling, Knowledge Codex recognition of a decoded tell, and a scripted onboarding tell. Phantom tells and false calm are not on this list: they are rejected by pillar (AT-17), permanently.

Seat state read (added by the author stage; flagged).** *Rule.* "Living player" (AT-6, AT-23) and the pod hold (AT-6, AT-22) need the Controller's `loco_state` per bound seat: a seat is *living* if `loco_state ≠ DEAD` (DOWNED counts as living) and *in pod* if `loco_state == IN_POD`; a seat in the pod can die there (user ruling D60, AT-22) and is living until `loco_state` reads DEAD *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. It creates no cycle (nothing in the Controller reads Attention, PCI:1010). The Controller owner is asked to repeat that `loco_state` is a published SIM read.

Diagnostics are inert.** *Rule.* A DIAGNOSTIC subscriber records, per run and per session, the counts of TELL entries, aborts and breaches, with every abort classified by its cause, **restraint** (the hold clause or the at-due level clause) or **void** (the departure void, AT-22), so a void never reads as restraint *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the published `tell_outcome` stays ABORTED for both, AT-16 is unchanged)*, ticks in each phase, the per-channel contribution (noise, light, power) of `I_run` over the ticks preceding each TELL entry, abort latency, and locus occupancy at breach. These values are never read by sim code, never published in `attention.view`, never shown to the player and are excluded from `state_hash`. They exist so a designer can answer "what crossed the line" without a meter in the game. (ADR candidate: diagnostics pipeline and export format.)

299	*The machine has four states. Every transition is evaluated inside `attention.step`, after the run's integration (AT-5) and in the order below; `post_restore` changes no `phase` and submits no command (the beacon is reconciled in the first `attention.step` run after a restore, AT-27). "Who may cause it" lists the only causes: no PLAYER-origin command, no other system's mutator and no timer outside the block can move the machine, apart from the SYSTEM-origin `attention_arm_tell` seam.*

304	|---|---|---|---|---|---|

404	## Formulas
405	
406	*Conventions (read first; every formula below uses them).* **Units.** The level is stored in **mAU** (64-bit integer); 1 AU = 1000 mAU = the noise of one walking tick (the Controller-owned registry row `NOISE_PER_TICK`, cited; its walk value defines the unit). `theta = ATT_THRESHOLD × 1000` mAU; `theta_HOLD = theta × HOLD_PM / 1000`; `L_CEIL = theta × L_CEIL_PM / 1000`; `TAU_ATT_TICKS` is written `tau` where space is short. All durations are ticks at `TICK_RATE`; a *run* is one `attention.step` execution at `T` a multiple of 6. **Integer rule (kernel determinism).** Everything that is hashed, persisted or replicated is integer: `floor()` is applied to non-negative operands only, `ceil(a / b)` for `a ≥ 0` is written `(a + b − 1) div b`, no float is used in the sim, and a float appears only in the closed-form *oracles* of the tests. **Weights** `W_L`, `W_P`, `W_S` are in micro-AU per unit per tick (1000 = 1 mAU per unit per tick), so `× 6 / 1000` turns a per-tick weight into mAU per run in one dimension (CQ-7: the systems-designer's single dimension; the game-designer's felt-target table is rationale and the playtest alternative, F-25). **Placeholders used in the worked examples** (all `[PLACEHOLDER]`, tuned in `assets/data/attention/`): `ATT_THRESHOLD` 6000 AU (`theta` 6,000,000), `HOLD_PM` 800 (`theta_HOLD` 4,800,000), `L_CEIL_PM` 1020 (`L_CEIL` 6,120,000), `TAU_ATT_TICKS` 1800, `ATT_MARGIN` 50 AU, `B_table` {ring 1: 300, ring 2: 450, ring 3: 550} AU, `U_TOOL` 4, `U_LOUD` 180, `W_L` 1000 for every lit kind, `W_P` 100, `W_S` 6000, `DARK_FLOOR_LOAD_W` 1500 W. **Cited, never re-derived:** the per-emitter term of EM D.12 (`section_emission`), KRN D.10 (`rng_derive`, `rng_int`), `ticks_for_seconds`, Graph D.11 (`fairness_gate`, `W_MIN_STEPS`), Save/Load's `autosave_gate`. **Evaluation order inside one run (the formulas depend on it):** (1) drain `pending_noise_mAU` into `I_noise` and `pending_ledger_mAU[s]` into the ledger inputs (F-1); (2) read `emitters()` and `power_use`, compute `nl_w` and `d_nl` and shift `nl_hist_w` (F-3, F-4); (3) integrate `L` (F-5); (4) update the ledger (F-6); (5) evaluate the phase logic on the integrated `L` (F-9, F-14, F-17) and advance `esc_ticks` while in TELL (F-12); (6) perform entry and exit actions (M17 deposits, `set_beacon`, F-18, F-19); (7) compute the beat schedule, tier and the published view (F-7, F-12, F-13). A TELL-entry run therefore publishes beat 0 (step 7) and runs no abort check on that same run.
407	
408	#### F-1. Noise intake (pending accumulator)
409	
410	The noise_intake formula is defined as:
411	
412	`pending_noise_mAU = min(L_CEIL, pending_noise_mAU + U[class] × 1000)` per accepted push; `pending_ledger_mAU[sec] = min(L_CEIL, pending_ledger_mAU[sec] + U[class] × 1000)` per accepted push whose source resolves, at push time, to a loaded section `sec`; at step (1): `I_noise = pending_noise_mAU` and `I_s(noise) = pending_ledger_mAU[s]`, then both are zeroed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; an accepted `BURDEN` push also sets the persisted flag `pending_burden`, which step (1) reads (it suspends this run's decay, F-5) and then clears *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*
413	
414	**Variables:**
415	
416	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
417	|---|---|---|---|---|
418	| `U[class]` | int AU | 0 to `U_LOUD` (knob range up to `ATT_THRESHOLD` ÷ 10) | the intake table (AT-3): `QUIET` 0; `WALK`, `RUN`, `CARRY` cited from `NOISE_PER_TICK` (walk 1 / run 4 / carry 1); `TOOL` = `U_TOOL`; `LOUD` = `U_LOUD`; `BURDEN` = `U_BURDEN` (F-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | attention units added by one push |
419	| `src` | PlayerId or object ref | transient | `push_stimulus(kind, source_ref, class)` | the attribution key, resolved to a section **at push time** (F-2) and then discarded; never persisted |
420	| `pending_noise_mAU` | int64 mAU | 0 to `L_CEIL` | block `attention.state` (persisted) | noise accumulated since the last run, for `I_noise`, whether or not its source could be placed; saturates at `L_CEIL` |
421	| `pending_ledger_mAU[sec]` | int64 mAU | 0 to `L_CEIL` per loaded section | block (persisted, sorted by `section_id`, loaded sections only) | the part of that noise attributed to a loaded section, for the ledger only (F-6) |
422	| `I_noise` | int64 mAU | 0 to `L_CEIL` | derived | the noise input of this run |
423	| `pending_burden` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)* | bool | 0/1 | block (persisted) | set by any accepted `BURDEN` push since the last run; read and cleared at step (1); when set, this run's decay is 0 (F-5) |
424	
425	**Output Range:** one source, one run: walking 6,000 mAU; running or carrying-while-running 24,000 mAU (PCI:560: 0 to 24 per run); a `TOOL` channel run 24,000 mAU; one `LOUD` push 180,000 mAU; holding a salvage carry 48,000 mAU moving (the CARRY walk push 6,000 plus `BURDEN` 42,000; any class, R5) and 42,000 mAU standing still *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The saturation at `L_CEIL` changes nothing below the ceiling (the level is clamped there anyway, F-5) and gives the overflow edge case a defined, bounded result. It binds only for a storm: one `LOUD` push is about 3 percent of `L_CEIL` at the placeholders, so it takes 34 of them in a single run to reach it, and no real source does; the earlier per-source clamp could never bind and is dropped (the review found it unreachable), which is why AC-AT-12 uses a synthetic storm. A `pending_ledger_mAU[s]` whose section became unloaded between the push and the step (a same-tick departure) is dropped and counted in `dropped_unattributed` at step (1), so AT-2's "no ledger entry for a dormant section" holds on that run too. An unknown class adds 0 and increments a counter.
426	**Example:** the player runs for 6 ticks and a cut completes in the same run: `24,000 + 180,000 = 204,000` mAU enter `pending_noise_mAU` (and the same into `pending_ledger_mAU` of the player's section). A 180-tick patch (`TOOL` pushed once per accrued tick) pushes `180 × 4 × 1000 = 720,000` mAU = 720 AU (IA D.9: equal to running for the same 180 ticks, four times walking). A `RUN` push of 24,000 mAU from a foot origin in a dormant section adds 24,000 to `pending_noise_mAU` and nothing to `pending_ledger_mAU`.
427	
428	#### F-2. Source-to-section attribution (feeds the ledger, not the level)
429	
430	The source_attribution formula is defined as:
431	
432	`section(src) = actor_section(src)` for a PlayerId source (foot-origin lookup); `section_of(src)` for an object source, both evaluated **at push time** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; `emitter.section_id` for light; the `power_use` section for power; a push whose section is dormant or unknown is dropped from the ledger (it stays in `pending_noise_mAU`) and counted
433	
434	**Variables:**
435	
436	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
437	|---|---|---|---|---|
438	| `actor_section(actor_id)` | section id | loaded sections | Ship Body read *(Body is Designed, 2026-10-27)* | the section holding the actor's foot origin |
439	| `section_of(ref)` | section id | loaded sections | Layout / owning system | the section of an object source |
440	| `dropped_unattributed` | int counter | 0 to unbounded | DIAGNOSTIC | pushes dropped because the section was dormant or unknown |
441	
442	**Output Range:** a loaded section id or a counted drop. A drop removes the push from the **ledger only**; the push still counts toward `I_noise` and `L` (the web hears a sound whose source it cannot place; the level is the world's, the locus is a choice). **Example:** the player in derelict A (`sec_a_2`) pushes `RUN` for 6 ticks: 24,000 mAU enter `pending_noise_mAU` and 24,000 mAU enter `pending_ledger_mAU[sec_a_2]`, which feeds `ledger[sec_a_2]` at step (4) (F-6).
443	
444	#### F-3. Light stimulus
445	
446	The light_stimulus formula is defined as:
447	
448	`I_light[s] = ( Σ_{e in emitters(s)} W_L[kind_e] × floor(output_pm_e × reach_px_e / 1000) × 6 ) div 1000`, and `I_light = Σ_s I_light[s]`
449	
450	**Variables:**
451	
452	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
453	|---|---|---|---|---|
454	| `W_L[kind]` | int (micro-AU per unit per tick) | 0 to 4000; 1000 for `BEAM`, `FIXTURE`, `NODE_LANTERN`, `DEPLOYABLE`; `FAULT_GLOW` 1000 in CALM and TELL and **0** in BREACH and SUBSIDING; `BEACON` **0** always (lint) | `assets/data/attention/weights` | the per-kind weight |
455	| `output_pm_e` | int | 0 to 1000 | emitter record (`emitters()`) | the emitter's steady output |
456	| `reach_px_e` | int px | 8 to 384 (EM shape table) | emitter record | the emitter's current reach |
457	| `floor(output_pm_e × reach_px_e / 1000)` | int | 0 to 384 | **cited: EM D.12 per-emitter term** | the Emitter State's own term, never re-derived |
458	| `kind_e` | enum | the closed `emitter_kind` list | emitter record | selects the weight |
459	| `emitters(s)` | list | at most `MAX_EMITTERS` in the world | Emitter State | every emitter of loaded section `s`, lit or not as the record reports `output_pm` |
460	| `I_light` | int64 mAU | 0 to 884,736 per run at the weight cap | derived | light input of this run |
461	
462	**Output Range:** 0 with no lit emitter. At the placeholder weights the maximum is `96 × 384 × 1000 × 6 div 1000 = 221,184` mAU per run (221 AU, `MAX_EMITTERS` emitters all at output 1000 and reach 384); 884,736 at the weight cap 4000. The owner's beam is counted **once**, from the emitter list at apex value; `lux_pm` is never read as a stimulus and `probe()` is never called (EM-21, EM-27). `served_pm` is not a stimulus: it reaches Attention as light through `output_pm`.
463	**Example:** the owner's wide beam (output 1000, reach 288, term 288), three home fixtures (1000, 144) and the cryo EMERGENCY lamp (1000, 144) all in one section: `(1000 × (288 + 4 × 144) × 6) div 1000 = (1000 × 864 × 6) div 1000 = 5,184` mAU per run. A live glowstick (1000, 96) adds `576` mAU per run; the stack cap `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` (four) adds 2,304: light is a spend, never a safe state.
464	*Derivation of `W_L[BEAM]` = 1000:* the wide beam's term 288 at weight 1000 is 288 mAU per tick, about 0.29 of a walking tick; running plus the beam from `L = B` settles toward `B + 4,288 × 1800 mAU` and crosses `theta` in 2,412 ticks (40 s) in the integer model (R4's calibration "about 45 s" is the same order); walking alone settles `1 AU × tau` = 1,800 AU above `B`, 30 percent of `theta`.
465	
466	#### F-4. Power stimulus
467	
468	The power_stimulus formula is defined as:
469	
470	`nl_w[s] = max(0, draw_w − lamps_lit_w)`; `d_nl[s] = nl_w[s] − nl_hist_w[s][4]` (the value five runs ago); `I_power[s] = ( W_P × nl_w[s] × 6 ) div 1000 + ( W_S × max(0, d_nl[s]) × 6 ) div 1000`; then `nl_hist_w[s]` shifts by one and `nl_w[s]` is stored at index 0; a loaded section with no entry (boot, wake, a restore that lacks it) is seeded `nl_hist_w[s][0..4] = nl_w[s]` before the first read; `W_N × noisy_w` is reserved at `W_N` = 0. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (C11 closed against LS-19: no `beacon_w`, no `beacon_step_w`, no read of `delta_w_last5`)
471	
472	**Variables:**
473	
474	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
475	|---|---|---|---|---|
476	| `W_P` | int (micro-AU per W per tick) | 0 to 300; placeholder 100 | data | steady non-lamp draw weight ("surplus draw is never free", LSG:794) |
477	| `W_S` | int (micro-AU per W per tick) | 0 to 20000; placeholder 6000 | data | transient (inrush) weight (the hiding verb's cost, LSG:809) |
478	| `draw_w` | int W | 0 to 10,000 per section | `power_use(section_id)` (LS-19: total served W, lamps and inrush included, battery charge excluded) | the section's total served load this step |
479	| `lamps_lit_w` | int W | 0 to `draw_w` | `power_use` (LS-19: served W of LOAD subtype LAMP, including any LAMP node such as `bcn_main`) | subtracted so a lamp is counted once, as light (EM-27) |
480	| `nl_w` | int W | 0 to 10,000 | derived: `max(0, draw_w − lamps_lit_w)` | the non-lamp draw |
481	| `nl_hist_w[s][0..4]` | 5 × int W | 0 to 10,000 each | block `attention.state` (persisted per loaded section, sorted by `section_id`; AT-1) | the last five runs' `nl_w`, oldest at index 4; seeded flat when a section loads, wakes or is restored without an entry |

The cold start of the whole tier 0 and 1 branch **with its lamps off** at `INRUSH_PM` 1500 (the Graph's data, default 1500 permille over `INRUSH_STEPS` 5 steps) takes `nl_w` from 0 to 1,500 W and gives `(6000 × 1500 × 6) div 1000 = 54,000` mAU through `W_S` for each of five runs = 270 AU in total (4.5 percent of `theta`), plus the steady `W_P` share. The ceiling is `W_P` 116 at ring 3 with the two wake glows (each +1 adds 2.7 AU to `x_dark` at 1,500 W and the ring-3 slack is 12 AU in level terms).
489	
490	#### F-5. The integrator (registry: `attention_integrator`)
491	
492	The attention_integrator formula is defined as:
493	
494	`dec = 0` if `pending_burden` was set when this run drained its pending input (a salvage carry is held aboard a non-home locus body and not `IN_POD`, F-26, AT-3 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*), else `dec = max(0, (6 × (L − B) + tau − 1) div tau)`; `L' = min(L_CEIL, max(B, L + I_run − dec))`; `I_run = I_noise + I_light + I_power` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5: the decay suspension)*
495	
496	**Variables:**
497	
498	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
499	|---|---|---|---|---|
500	| `L` | int64 mAU | `B` to `L_CEIL` | block (persisted) | the level before this run |
501	| `B` | int64 mAU | 300,000 to about 724,000 at the placeholder rows (about 594,000 with the two wake glows) | F-8 | the baseline for the current ring |
502	| `tau` | int ticks | 300 to 3600 (at least 300 by IR-3), placeholder 1800 | `TAU_ATT_TICKS` | the single memory constant |
503	| `I_run` | int64 mAU | at least 0 | F-1, F-3, F-4 | this run's input |
504	| `L_CEIL` | int64 mAU | `theta` to 1.1 `theta` | data (`L_CEIL_PM`, ADDITION X1 adopted by checkpoint ruling CQ-2 and approved at the CD-GDD-ALIGN gate) | the saturation level |
505	| `dec` | int64 mAU | 0 to `(L_CEIL − B) × 6 / 1800 + 1` | derived | the ceiling decay of this run, computed on the **pre-input** `L` |
506	
507	**Output Range:** `[B, L_CEIL]` = [300,000, 6,120,000] mAU at ring 1. `dec` is at least 1 whenever `L > B`, so with zero input the level reaches `B` **exactly** (the integer truncation stall of LSG:464 cannot occur); with large input it saturates at `L_CEIL`. Under a constant input `r` (mAU per tick) the steady level is `L_ss = B + r × tau` (the per-run fixed point has `dec = 6r`); while a salvage carry is held aboard a non-home locus body (not `IN_POD`, AT-3) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* there is no steady state, and the level rises by `I_run` per run until `L_CEIL` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*. If a ring change raises `B` above `L`, then `L − B` is negative, `dec` is 0 and `L` is lifted to `B` in the same run; if `B` falls, `L` decays toward the new floor.
508	**Upper-bound lint on theta** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (`reckless_crossing`): the sustained verbs (run, or the tool channel, with the beam) inflow `r_sustain = 4,000 + 288 = 4,288` mAU per tick, so the level can never exceed `B + r_sustain × tau` = 8,018 AU at ring 1 and a theta near that is unreachable. The lint is `t_cross(theta, r_sustain, from B) ≤ CROSS_MAX_TICKS` (placeholder 4,320, 72 s), run through the integer F-5: theta 6,000 crosses in 2,412 ticks, 7,000 in 3,642, 7,200 (the game-designer alternative) in 4,038, 7,300 in 4,272 (the edge), 7,400 in 4,542 (fails), 8,000 in 10,872 (fails) and 8,100 never. So the safe range of `ATT_THRESHOLD` is 5,816 to 7,300 AU (AC-AT-126).

933	`I_burden(tick) = U_BURDEN × 1000 if a salvage carry is held AND the holder's body is not the home body AND loco_state ≠ IN_POD, else 0` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: the location gate of AT-3)*, pushed by the Controller once per tick as class `BURDEN`; a run's burden is the sum over its six ticks (42,000 mAU for six ticks of holding at `U_BURDEN` 7), entering `pending_noise_mAU` and the holder's `pending_ledger_mAU` through F-1; the only new state is the flag `pending_burden`, which suspends that run's decay (F-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5: salvage scope and the decay suspension)*

948	
949	**Derivation of `U_BURDEN`.** Integer F-5 over Boarding's lit golden schedule (walk-in 312 ticks at 1 AU, door attempts 60 idle, the cut 240 ticks at `U_TOOL` with `U_LOUD` on its last tick, the pickup 12 idle, then the carry at the CARRY push plus the burden, then 30 idle ticks holding at the console), beam 288 and lit home 766 mAU per tick, from `L0`. 980	## Edge Cases
981	
982	*Each entry reads "If [condition]: [exact outcome]. [rationale]" and names the diagnostic or reason code where one exists. Entries are grouped by theme; `E-n` ids are stable references for the Acceptance Criteria. Rule ids are `AT-n`, formulas `F-n`. Provisional entries say which sibling or undesigned system they depend on.*
983	
984	#### Intake, level and bounds
985	
986	- **E-1. If `push_stimulus` is called with an unknown `class` or a `kind` other than `NOISE`**: it adds nothing, increments the unknown-class counter and returns; the call never rejects or asserts (Class B: clamp, never reject; AT-3). Reserved kinds are rejected by lint at authoring, not at run time.
987	- **E-2. If a `QUIET` push arrives**: nothing is added to `pending_noise_mAU` or any `pending_ledger_mAU` entry *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the field is `pending_noise_mAU`, F-1)* and the `QUIET` counter increments. The class exists so Interaction can declare a silent verb explicitly (IA-33).
988	- **E-3. If a push's source resolves to a dormant or unknown section** (an object in a cut-away section, a foot origin in no section): the push still counts toward `I_noise` and so toward `L` (it is added to `pending_noise_mAU` only), nothing is written to `pending_ledger_mAU` (so no ledger key ever exists for an unloaded section), and `dropped_unattributed` increments (F-2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The web hears a sound it cannot place; the level is the world's and the locus is only a choice.
989	- **E-4. If many pushes stack in one run** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (six seats each pushing `LOUD` reach 1,080,000 mAU, 18 percent of `L_CEIL`, and saturate nothing; only a synthetic storm of 35 or more `LOUD` pushes at the placeholder `U_LOUD` does): `pending_noise_mAU` and each `pending_ledger_mAU[s]` saturate at `L_CEIL`, `I_run` is bounded by `L_CEIL` plus the F-3 and F-4 maxima, and `L'` clamps at `L_CEIL`; all arithmetic stays far below 2^63 (F-1, F-5). The saturation changes nothing below the ceiling.
990	- **E-5. If `power_use` is absent for a loaded section**: `I_power[s]` is 0, the diagnostic `ATT_POWER_ABSENT` is logged once per process, and `served_pm` is **not** substituted (it already enters as light). Nothing else changes (F-4).
991	- **E-6. If `emitters()` is empty, every section is dormant or no section is loaded**: `I_light` and `I_power` are 0, no ledger exists, `L` decays to `B` exactly (F-5), and a TELL cannot start (lint: `B < theta` at every ring).
992	- **E-7. If 96 emitters (`MAX_EMITTERS`) are live**: `I_light` is at most 221,184 mAU per run at weight 1000 and 884,736 at the weight cap (F-3), and `L` pins at `L_CEIL`; a TELL then starts at the first legal run. The MVP slice (five home compartments) cannot reach this; a Vertical Slice growth that does (about 29 powered fixtures reach the hold line at rest at the game-designer's K1 values) is a tripwire for the lint `survivable_dark_floor`, which fails at authoring, and for the open question on per-section lamp switching (GD-15). "Lights you left on" must stay a decision and not become an inevitability.
993	- **E-8. If a ring change raises `B` above `L`** (descent): `L` is lifted to `B` in the same run (`dec` is 0 because `L − B` is negative), `level_pm` reads 0, and no TELL starts unless `L ≥ theta`. The held-ring rule (AT-6) applies while a seat is `IN_POD`.
994	- **E-9. If `B` falls** (a return to the home ring): `L` decays toward the new `B` at a rate proportional to the excess; there is no free reset, because the level is absolute and the baseline only a floor.
995	- **E-10. If `theta ≤ B` for any ring, or a `B_table` row breaks F-15 or F-16**: boot refuses (the data lint of AT-6, evaluated with `N_GLOW_DARK` = the glows authored active at wake, F-16). A division by zero in `level_pm` and a ring on which restraint cannot end a tell are both data errors caught before play.
996	- **E-11. If `L` equals `theta_HOLD` exactly**: it is not below the line (the comparison is strict `<`), so no abort counting happens and, on the due run, the breach commits. The boundary is deterministic and chosen to favour consequence over relief.
997	
998	#### Simultaneous rules and timing boundaries
999	
1000	- **E-12. If a `LOUD` push lands in the run that crosses `theta`**: it is part of that run's `I_run`; the run enters TELL, draws `tell_len ≥ TELL_DRAW_LO`, and publishes beat 0 in the same run. The breach cannot occur before `tell_start_T + tell_len`; there is no instant-breach path (AT-8).
1001	- **E-13. If two crossings occur in one run** (two `LOUD` pushes in co-op): one TELL, one `tell_epoch` increment and one RNG draw (the counter advances by exactly 1).
1002	- **E-14. If `L ≥ theta` while `T < refract_until_T` or `T < rearm_until_T`**: the phase stays CALM, `L` keeps integrating up to `L_CEIL`, `level_pm` reads 1000, and the first run at or after the later timer enters TELL with beat 0 and `tell_elapsed` 0. No catch-up elapsed time is credited, so a long wait never shortens the tell.
1003	- **E-15. If TELL entry falls exactly on `T == refract_until_T`** (or `rearm_until_T`): it is legal (the guard is `≥`).
1004	- **E-16. If the abort counter reaches `ABORT_HOLD_TICKS` on the same run as `T ≥ breach_due_T`**: the abort wins and is one transition (`tell_outcome = ABORTED`, no STRESS, no beacon). A run that is both "due" and "under the line" is an abort, never a breach.
1005	- **E-17. If `L` drops below `theta_HOLD` and rises back before `ABORT_HOLD_TICKS` elapses**: `below_hold_runs` resets to 0; only the at-due path remains. One dip does not abort.
1006	- **E-18. If the clear-hold clause and `BREACH_MAX_TICKS` are both satisfied on one run**: one transition, BREACH to SUBSIDING; deposits stop on that run (F-18).
1007	- **E-19. If `attention_arm_tell` is called outside CALM**: it is rejected with reason `NOT_CALM` and changes nothing. Inside CALM it enters TELL at the next run, clamps `tell_len` to `[TELL_MIN_TICKS, TELL_MAX_TICKS]` (100 becomes 600), does not honour the two timers and does not consume `rng_counter` (F-9, F-10).
1008	- **E-20. If the beam is strobed in step with the six-tick cadence**: light is sampled once per run, so the sampled state can be systematically off. The Controller adapter's toggle debounce (EM:720) owns the defence; Attention adds no cooldown and no sim-side rule (the EM text says the sim adds none). A person cannot phase-lock to a sample tick they cannot see; only a macro could, and a macro strobing the beam off at every sample is paying the lit-only verb price (IA-6) for nothing.
1009	
1010	#### Tell, abort and the pod
1011	
1012	- **E-21. If a player is DOWNED during a TELL**: the tell continues; their noise stops (a downed seat pushes nothing); their beam is whatever the Emitter State reports; a DOWNED seat counts as living for the baseline ring and the pod hold (AT-31). The tell is world-level, never player-level.
1013	- **E-22. If every living player dies during a TELL**: the death stub restores the newest verified autosave (SL-7) and Attention rolls back with it (WORLD scope), including `rng_counter`, `tell_len` and every timer, so a tell already drawn in the snapshot replays its length and beats exactly (no reroll), while every tell drawn after the restore takes the new `restore_epoch` key and so does not replay the length the dead run met (user ruling D16, AT-8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
1014	- **E-23. If a player hops by pod during a TELL** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(creative-director ruling on OQ-AT-12; **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions)**, including that a home-ship-locus tell is not voidable by hopping)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the tell clock continues, the bed and beats are unchanged and `held_ring` keeps `B` until arrival (a departure never aborts the tell early). If the locus body is not the home-ship body and every seat recorded in it at TELL entry has left it by the due run (`locus_vacated`), the due-run decision is an **abort**, not a breach: TELL → CALM, `tell_outcome = ABORTED`, no STRESS, no beacon, `rearm_until_T` set, the release cue plays. The departed derelict going dormant (WM-24) does not trigger the AT-14 fallback, because the void is resolved first; the breach is never moved onto the home ship the player escaped to. If a living seat stays in the locus body, the breach proceeds on that body. A home-ship locus is not voidable (E-27 and the Moment B variant: no pod escape from a home-ship breach); Web Map's ASK-A4 (hold the transfer while no seat is aboard home) is declined and the home-locus breach proceeds as ruled, and the case with nobody aboard the home ship is E-73 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Only if the locus held no living seat at TELL entry and Web Map keeps it loaded (a berthed derelict) does the breach proceed on the recorded `locus_body`, ending under X10 at `BREACH_MIN_TICKS` (F-17). X10 is reachable at MVP only through that berthed case; the departed-derelict form is fixture-only.
1015	- **E-73. If the locus is the home ship and no living seat is aboard the home body at TELL entry, at BREACH entry, or at both** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (reachable without contrivance: residual noise at home, a weld or a run, followed by a sortie before the home ledger has decayed; a hop that voided a tell (a void leaves the level unrelieved, `ABORT_RELIEF_PM` 1000, AT-10) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; or the quiet-crew case of Moment C, where the lit home ship's ledger out-weighs a still player elsewhere): `tell_occupants_at_entry` and `locus_occupants_at_entry` are recorded empty; `locus_vacated` is false because the body is the home ship (F-14), so the due run is decided by the level alone and the breach is never voided; clause (iii) of AT-12 and the X10 clause (iv) both require a non-home body, so neither applies, and the breach ends by (i) `BREACH_MAX_TICKS` or (ii) `CLEAR_HOLD_TICKS` of quiet after `BREACH_MIN_TICKS` (the level is global, so the crew ends it by going quiet wherever they are). `set_beacon(on)` is submitted at T+1 as for any breach and sweeps on the empty home ship; STRESS lands on the home body in bursts; `TellAudit` records each deposit as an ordinary harm event inside a told breach's locus body, and the contract holds (F-23): the tell was perceivable to every living player through the non-positional bed, and Audio's alarm pulse is heard wherever they are (AA-20), so only the beacon goes unseen. A player who comes home mid-breach is not in `locus_occupants_at_entry`, changes no end clause and meets the breach (and Horror's REACH if they linger, HE-F16). **The player-facing price, stated honestly:** the noise made at home, or the lights left on at home (Moment C), comes due on the home ship whether or not anyone is there; it is the consequence of the OQ-AT-12 ruling and it was told. Web Map's request to hold the transfer until a seat is aboard (ASK-A4) is declined (AT-22). Criterion: AC-AT-46 clause 4.
1016	- **E-24. If a tell is the shortest possible** (`attention_arm_tell` with 600): the beats follow F-12 (at least 4 in the window on any level trajectory, 5 when the level stays at or above the hold line) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, the tier follows F-13, and the BREACH-or-abort decision still occurs at the due run. R10 (b) binds at this length, and at ring 3 with the placeholder dark load it holds with 24 ticks of slack, 6 with the two wake glows (F-15).
1017	- **E-25. If the player enters TELL at the highest possible level and does everything right** (stops, sets any cargo down, kills the lamp, opens the breaker): the abort completes inside the shortest tell in play (F-15b slack 144 to 174 ticks, 126 at ring 3 with the two wake glows) but only if the reaction allowance holds; a player who reacts after `REACT_ALLOW_TICKS` forfeits the abort on the shortest draws. That is the stated price of attention, not a defect (AT-10).
1018	- **E-26. If the player stops everything at `theta` and later tries to resume the interrupted cut**: the abort completes 594 ticks after the stop on a clean ship (F-15b), 6 ticks inside `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`, a window no player can use, and 606 ticks with the two shipped wake glows, past it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the partial is **always** forfeited and the cut restarts from zero *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Restraint costing the partial is a legitimate price (AT stance on Moment A).
1019	
1020	#### Breach, locus, STRESS and the beacon
1021	
1022	- **E-27. If the locus section is cut away or goes dormant during TELL or BREACH** *(provisional — Assembly; Web Map is designed)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (a departure that empties a non-home locus is resolved by the void of AT-22 first and never reaches this fallback: during a TELL the fallback is suppressed from the first run at which `locus_vacated` holds, so the dormancy of a departed derelict at run N does not re-point the locus before the due run N+k): the locus falls back to the home-ship's lowest `section_id`, `locus_body` is recomputed, the tell is not restarted and `tell_remaining` is unchanged; TellAudit records `LOCUS_FALLBACK(epoch, old_body, new_body, tick)` and the contract evaluates later deposits against the new body (F-23, AT-15); STRESS already armed on a cut-away section lapses on its own hold. **A cut moves the locus and never launders Attention** (Modular Ship Assembly E-26, T15 A1): the level `L`, `phase`, the timers and `tell_epoch` are unchanged by the cut, and only the cut-away section's ledger entry is dropped. In BREACH, a dormancy caused by a pod departure that empties a non-home locus is resolved by the AT-22 departure test first (it ends the breach, WM:87), so the fallback applies only when the breach is not ended that run.
1023	- **E-28. If two sections tie in `ledger_mAU` at TELL entry**: the lowest `section_id` is the locus (a deterministic tie-break, F-6).
1024	- **E-29. If a STRESS deposit is dropped because `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` is saturated in the run** (Horror deposits by path (a), Class B `deposit_trace` from the `horror.step` hook, so Attention claims no first place, C22, Horror HE-28): Attention cannot observe the drop (the mutator is Class B and returns no rejection), so the section is unstressed until the next burst run, one burst period (`STRESS_REFRESH_RUNS` × 6 = 1,800 ticks) later at most. Missing STRESS is never an unannounced harm (STRESS only amplifies failures that were already ticking), so the tell-window contract is not violated; the guarantee against the drop is Horror's must-repeat budget of at most `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP − STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` per run.
1025	- **E-30. If `set_beacon` is rejected** (`NOT_LIVE` because the home-ship's power is dead, `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_BEACON`) or expires at `max_age_ticks`: the machine proceeds (the bed, STRESS and the failing hardware carry the breach), the failure is logged once, and the command is retried once per run while `beacon_retry_left > 0` (`BEACON_RETRY_RUNS` placeholder 20). A dead ship's beacon is dark (EM:200); this is intended.
1026	- **E-31. If the beacon's own draw reaches the power channel in BREACH or SUBSIDING** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: it cannot. `bcn_main` is a LAMP node, so its 20 W and its switch-on step sit inside `lamps_lit_w` and `nl_w` excludes them (F-4, LS-19); the alarm cannot hold `L` above `theta_HOLD` and delay the exit it is tested against. If a future Graph revision stopped counting `bcn_main` as a lamp, the 20 W would add 12 mAU per run steady plus 720 mAU per run for five runs (`(6000 × 20 × 6) div 1000`): the lint `BEACON_NOT_LAMP` (AC-AT-63) reports it, and it is never a silent behaviour change.
1027	- **E-32. If the beacon is switched on at BREACH entry and the listener or the nearest player is on a derelict**: no visible beacon reaches them (one beacon, on the home-ship, DA-24); the held rim, the failing hardware and Audio's alarm pulse on its fallback clock carry the breach (the tell bed ended at BREACH entry, Audio AA-20), and under reduced flashing the beacon is a static mark (AT-18, AT-24).
1028	- **E-33. If a breach's locus body is a non-home body with no living player at BREACH entry** (a lit derelict kept loaded by a berth after the crew left it; X10 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*): BREACH ends at `BREACH_MIN_TICKS`; STRESS lapses on the Graph's hold; the beacon goes off at SUBSIDING entry. The clause is evaluated at entry only, so a player who arrives later is not retroactively rescued and, not being in `locus_occupants_at_entry`, does not trigger clause (iii) by leaving; clause (iii) is for an occupant recorded at entry.
1029	- **E-34. If STRESS outlasts SUBSIDING** (tail of 606 to 2,400 ticks, F-18): no new Attention exogenous call occurs in CALM (the contract predicate is satisfied by the existing arming), and the ship keeps failing faster for the tail. This is the intended "spreading wrongness, then silence" (LSG:986); no Attention surface shows the tail and `phase == CALM` is never an all-clear (Audio must repeat).
1030	- **E-35. If a breach lands on a clean ship** (no endogenous fault in the locus body): STRESS multiplies nothing and the breach is nearly a non-event. This cannot be the normal MVP case: every possible locus body on MVP derelicts A and B is authored with at least one active overload or fatigue fault (AT-11, the gate's content requirement; AC-AT-117), and Horror's single MVP behaviour wired to BREACH is a blocking dependency. A body the player has repaired clean is their earned result, and `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT` is not raised to hide it.
1031	- **E-36. If the cryo bay (the EMERGENCY fixture `fx_cryo_lamp`) holds the locus or the player is in it during a tell**: the lamp counts as light in F-3, never gutters and never carries a tier (LO-20, DA-23); filaments and the audio bed carry the tell, and no outcome changes.
1032	- **E-37. If the locus body has more sections than one burst can cover** (`S > STRESS_REFRESH_BURST_RUNS × STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN`): the second lint of F-18 fails at authoring; at run time the cursor wraps and the remaining sections wait for the next burst. The MVP's largest body (14) is covered by 24.
1033	
1034	#### Degenerate strategies
1035	
1036	- **E-38. If the player stands still in the dark indefinitely, holding no cargo** (CR-DOM; with cargo see E-66) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the level settles at `x_dark` (F-16), no tell can start, and nothing progresses, because every repair, cut and weld verb is lit-only (IA-6), the loops run on the survival load that is part of `x_dark`, and the breaker's inrush is the price of ever lighting up again. The web is not toothless: the cost of restraint is time, air and heat, not an Attention penalty. A playtest tripwire (abort share above 85 percent among experienced players, AC-GD-16) is the signal that the freeze has become a ritual.
1037	- **E-39. If a player baits tells and aborts them for free** (tell farming): an abort leaves `L` unchanged (`ABORT_RELIEF_PM` 1000), so the next crossing costs the same effort as the first, and `TELL_REARM_TICKS` forbids re-entry for 600 ticks. The knob `ABORT_RELIEF_PM` below 1000 exists only as a lever if playtests show chained-abort fatigue.
1038	- **E-40. If a player throws a glowstick into an empty section to steer the locus** (CR-LURE) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* the stick's light enters that section's ledger like any light (F-2, F-6): 96 mAU per tick, a steady ledger of 172,800 mAU (691,200 at the stack cap of four), against steady ledgers of 2,318,400 for a player walking with the beam, 518,400 for one standing still with the beam and about 1,379,000 for the lit idle home ship. **Noise dominates the ledger, and a lit stick left alone wins the locus only against sections quieter still** (a full stack out-weighs a player standing still with only the beam, and only while the home ship is dark). A stick that lands in another section of the same body changes nothing, because STRESS covers the whole locus body (AT-14); it can move the breach only by landing in a different loaded body. The landing push (180,000 mAU, a one-shot `LOUD`, IA-33) is attributed to the section where it lands and decays out of that ledger with `tau`; the global level rose by the same push. A playtest watch item together with CR-DOM; `LOCUS_OCC_PREF_PM` is the lever.
1039	- **E-41. If a player splits a long job across pauses to launder noise**: IR-3 keeps `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` at most twice `TAU_ATT_TICKS`, so a job split across the TTL retains about 72 percent of its first block; there is no pause length that resets the level to `B` except the decay itself.
1040	- **E-42. If a player skims the threshold** (repeated entry and abort at the edge): the 600-tick rearm and the unchanged level make each cycle cost a full decay and a full re-approach; onset cues cannot chatter (AUD X10 adopted).
1041	- **E-43. If a player runs continuously with the beam on**: the level crosses `theta` from `B` in 2,412 ticks (40 s) in the integer model and the tell begins; this is the intended punishment for refusing the one noise readout the game gives (the footsteps).
1042	- **E-44. If an Assembly weld completes in a derelict welded to the home ship**: **zero** `LOUD` is pushed at weld completion (IA-33 declares `LOUD` one-shots at cut completion, seam-cut DONE, vent apply and throw landing only; a weld completion is none of these; the weld's cost to Attention is its accrued `TOOL` ticks), Assembly pushes nothing at MVP, and the locus body now spans both, so the next breach shares STRESS across the welded body. A seam-cut reaching DONE pushes exactly one `LOUD`, from Interaction (Modular Ship Assembly T14 C5).
1043	- **E-65. If a player throttles** (alternates short loud bursts with long stillness so the level hovers under `theta` and no tell ever starts) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: no tell, no breach and no Horror content ever occurs, `breaches per session` falls toward 0 (below the registered 3 to 8) and the build is toothless in the way a hidden-timer design is not. E-38 covers the pure freeze, whose cost is air, heat and time; throttling is cheaper because it keeps working. **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), OQ-AT-27: lever (a), the calibration route**, delivered by the carry-burden term of F-26 (the weights and `ATT_THRESHOLD` are retained; an ordinary haul now reaches `theta`), so a hauling sortie cannot be throttled under the line; throttle play on work that carries nothing stays a playtest watch item behind the AC-AT-80 gate. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **A second route to near-zero breaches, from the rulings themselves:** the departure void (OQ-AT-12) plus the carry burden (X3) make walking to the pod the near-dominant answer to any derelict tell when the pod is within about 37 tiles unladen (about 19 tiles carrying; 900 ticks at 2 and 1 px per tick) (a hop voids the breach and keeps the cut and the haul; an abort forfeits the partial), and a void leaves the level unrelieved but the level decays through the pod, because the burden stops at the pod door (AT-3): on the reference carry it arrives home at 4,511,793 mAU lit (3,734,036 with no pod intake), below `theta_HOLD` 4,800,000, so no home tell opens (Boarding EC-BS-63, AC-BS-123 (e)); a hop made earlier in a tell, at a higher level, can be followed by a home-ship tell once the rearm ends, and AC-AT-134 measures how often (Moment C, E-73) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Restraint aborts and breaches then both trend toward zero, which threatens Pillar 3 and the AC-AT-80 band. It is a consequence of two user rulings, not a reason to reopen either; it is not retuned silently: AC-AT-134 measures it and OQ-AT-36 is decided (leave it, measured; R21) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R21)*. The levers considered, none of which may become a hidden timer: (a) calibrate the weights and `ATT_THRESHOLD` so an ordinary sortie reaches `theta` (the AC-AT-57 harness picks), (b) the Vertical Slice per-ring gain on light and power (AT-6), (c) a Graph-side cost that grows with time spent working (air, heat), which is visible and diegetic. Detection: the AC-AT-80 breaches-per-session gate.
1044	
1045	#### Carry, freeze and the user rulings of 2026-10-27 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
1046	
1047	- **E-66. If the player holds cargo and stands still, in the light or in the dark** *(user ruling X3)*: the Controller keeps pushing `BURDEN` every tick while the cargo is salvage (F-26), and the decay is suspended while it is held (F-5), so standing still is not a way to wait the web out *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*. Lit, with the beam on and the home ship lit, the level crosses `theta` in 360 ticks after the cut and 540 ticks from the lit-idle level; fully dark (beam off, home dark, start at the 829 AU dark floor) it crosses in 714 ticks. The escapes are the ones the rules name: set the cargo down (`drop` is free and exempt from the lit rule; the item stays where it fell and re-taking it needs light, IA-28; re-taking the same item, or carrying it back aboard a non-home body, before the rearm ends cancels the rearm, AT-10 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*) or ride the tell out. Cargo carried at home, or the player's own kit, is not salvage: it pushes no burden and suspends nothing. The freeze after the cut is priced, not free (OQ-BS-27). E-38's pure freeze (no cargo) is unchanged.
1048	- **E-67. If the level dips under `theta_HOLD` and climbs back before the abort** *(user ruling OQ-AT-25)*: `below_hold_runs` resets (E-17), `esc_ticks` stays where the dip left it and resumes from there, `tier` and the beat interval never fall, and beats keep publishing in real time at the frozen interval; one dip neither aborts the tell nor makes it worse.
1049	- **E-68. If a restore changes `restore_epoch`** *(user ruling D16)*: a tell already drawn in the snapshot keeps its `tell_len` and replays its beats; the next draw reads the stream at the kernel's `counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch`, so it differs from the one the earlier run met; `rng_counter` itself is restored exactly. Every death-stub restore advances the epoch, and so does a Continue (in-process or fresh-process) of any generation other than the newest Save & Quit generation, so a second death restore of the same autosave and a Continue of an autosave after a fresh process start both take a new epoch; Save/Load makes the advance durable in `slot_epoch.bin` before `request_restore`. A Continue of that newest `QUIT` generation carries the epoch and replays the same draws (R1 as amended by R13/R14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. A restore with the same epoch value pinned (the test harness) is hash-identical to uninterrupted play (AC-AT-22).
1050	- **E-69. If the last living seat dies in the pod** *(user ruling D60)*: no section contains a living player, `B` holds its last value (E-63) and the death handling restores an autosave (E-22); a seat that dies in the pod while another lives at home stops counting for `B` and the pod hold, and the departure clauses (AT-12 iii, AT-22) already held because its section had left `locus_body` (its `occ_gone` was set while it was `IN_POD` and is kept after death, F-14). A recorded seat that dies **inside** the locus body is the opposite case: it keeps counting as present, so a death never voids a tell or ends a breach early *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
1051	- **E-70. If the pod is berthed in the locus body, or in a derelict where nothing else is lit** *(user ruling X2)*: the DOCK_STATUS glow is lit, counts as light (F-3) and as unswitchable (F-16), and never carries a strand (AT-20); a site lit only by it is not eligible, so a deaf player in that derelict has no visual channel and the opt-in haptic pulse is theirs (AT-24).
1052	- **E-71. If a berth completes in the run that crosses `theta`, or while a tell runs** *(default applied, D59)*: the one `LOUD` push (180,000 mAU, 3 percent of `theta`) is part of that run's `I_run` like any other (E-12); it cannot open a tell from the lit-idle level on its own, and it is attributed to the home-ship console section, so it adds to that section's ledger and not to the derelict's.
1053	- **E-72. If the haptic pulse is on and the game restores, pauses or hitches** *(user ruling OQ-AT-1)*: the pulse fires on the `(tell_epoch, tell_beat)` change only, so a load fires none (transitions only, AT-27), a pause fires none and a hitch fires at most one pulse for the current pair (the dedupe of AC-AT-115).
1054	
1055	#### Save, restore and persistence
1056	
1057	- **E-45. If a snapshot is restored mid-TELL**: `rng_counter`, `tell_len`, `breach_due_T`, `tell_beat`, `esc_ticks`, `beat_next_off` and `below_hold_runs` restore, no length is redrawn, no onset cue replays (cues fire on transitions only), and the beat sequence is hash-identical to uninterrupted play (G4; AT-1, AT-27).
1058	- **E-46. If a snapshot is restored mid-BREACH**: `stress_next_burst_run` and `stress_pending_cursor` restore, bursts resume on schedule, and no deposit gap exceeds the coverage margin; the beacon is reconciled by the first run (E-48).
1059	- **E-47. If a snapshot lands on the `breach_due_T` run**: both the pre-run state (phase TELL) and the post-run state (phase BREACH) restore to an identical continuation, because the transition is inside one run and `phase` changes nowhere else.
1060	- **E-48. If `beacon_commanded` disagrees with the emitter's switch state after a restore** (a SYSTEM command pending at snapshot time is dropped on reload, KRN:593, :609): `post_restore` changes nothing and submits nothing; the first `attention.step` run after the restore compares the two and submits `set_beacon` only on a mismatch, with the usual `BEACON_RETRY_RUNS` retry. If they already agree, nothing is submitted (idempotent).
1061	- **E-49. If a save made in CALM with `tell_outcome = ABORTED`, or in BREACH, is loaded**: no onset, no breach-enter and no release cue plays (transition-only); the view carries the persisted `tell_outcome` and `tell_epoch`.
1062	- **E-50. If a loaded block holds an out-of-range value, an incoherent phase or an unknown section id**: restore returns a hard failure with the reason `ATTENTION_RESTORE_RANGE`, `_PHASE_INCOHERENT` or `_SECTION_UNKNOWN`; nothing is clamped and the load is refused (SL-15).
1063	- **E-51. If an autosave is due during a TELL**: Save/Load's gate reads `tell_active`, `tell_remaining` and `breach_phase`; because `breach_phase` reports TELL as CALM, FAIR mode stays live (C5). A state saved mid-TELL restores the full tell (`tell_len ≥ TELL_MIN_TICKS`), so the player is never saved into a shorter warning than the contract allows. The gate formula itself is Save/Load's.
1064	- **E-52. If the game is paused or the window loses focus**: sim `T` stops and Attention runs on `T` only; no wall time is read, so no catch-up burst of beats or decay occurs on resume (AT-28). The kernel never fast-forwards (`LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` = 0, ratified 2026-10-27 with the kernel batch, X13), so a hitch replays no missed sim ticks, and the per-catch-up-frame merge of PRESENTATION and DIAGNOSTIC notifications leaves one beat notification per poll, which is the dedupe AC-AT-115 already tests *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
1065	
1066	#### Hallucination interplay (the tell is a truth channel)
1067	
1068	- **E-53. If a phantom entity lunges at a low-sanity player** (class a) with no beat, no resolving filament and no beacon before it: TellAudit records nothing (there is no web-originated event), Attention does nothing, and the player has a cheap first check that costs attention (they must have been listening to the bed): "the web did not look up, so this is not the web" (AT-17). The boundary is honest: it rules out web-originated harm, not an entity's presence and not the crew; a real entity may stand in CALM (Horror's non-lethal presence outside BREACH is required), so the check never licenses ignoring what is seen.
1069	- **E-54. If a false system state shows a hull failing** (class b) while `phase` is CALM: no STRESS exists, the real gauge is unaffected, and `attention.view` still reports CALM; Attention reads no `PERCEPTION_OUT` value, so the lie cannot reach the machine (CR-12).
1070	- **E-55. If the Perception Filter or Sanity tries to remove, add, delay or alter a tell cue** (a filament, a bed beat): it is a lint failure (the Filter's write set must not contain an Attention cue; its anchor list includes the tell cues). The MVP has no phantom tell and no false calm (AT-17).
1071	- **E-56. If a crewmate appears as a horror and lethal friendly harm follows** (class c): friendly harm is Sanity's gate, not Attention's; Attention neither gates nor enables it. A crewmate's tool harm is player-originated and needs no tell; only a horror's lethal act on a crew body is audited by `tell_window_contract`, provisionally (R15).
1072	- **E-57. If a phantom emitter, a hallucinated beam or phantom loot exists in the player's view**: the emitter list holds real records only (EM-3 gives a record no phantom field), so phantom light adds nothing; taking phantom loot picks nothing up and pushes no noise. Real carry noise comes only from a real action.
1073	
1074	#### Co-op hooks (Vertical Slice; one machine at MVP)
1075	
1076	- **E-58. If two players stand in different rings** (VS-B): `B` uses the maximum ring over living players (F-8); each hears the non-positional bed; `tell_beat` is shared (`SHARED_SUMMARY`); the single level and the `source` tag keep per-player attribution a data change.
1077	- **E-59. If a downed crewmate's beam or a corpse could be a lantern**: noted only (EM:1121); it counts as an emitter if the Emitter State lists it, with no Attention rule of its own.
1078	- **E-60. If the locus body holds only some of the players**: STRESS and `exogenous_permitted` apply to the locus body alone; the other players still hear the bed (perceivable relative to every living player, AT-15) and the home-ship beacon, and are safe from the breach's STRESS unless their body is welded to the locus body.
1079	
1080	#### Absent or provisional neighbours
1081	
1082	- **E-61. If Web Map's ring is absent**: `ring_of` (registry, Web Map & Transit) resolves an absent or sub-1 ring to ring 1 with one log line per process (AT-6).
1083	- **E-62. If Ship Body's `actor_section` is unavailable for a seat** *(Body is Designed, 2026-10-27)*: that player's noise enters `I_noise` and the ledger drop of E-3 applies; the foot-origin lookup never blocks the machine. For the departure tests (the void, AT-22; clause (iii), AT-12) a recorded seat whose lookup is unavailable keeps its last `occ_gone` status, present if it never left, and one diagnostic is logged per epoch, so an unavailable lookup can never void a tell or end a breach by itself (F-14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
1084	- **E-63. If the Controller's `loco_state` is DEAD for every seat**: no section "contains a living player", so `B` holds its last value; the death handling then restores an autosave (E-22). Attention never invents a ring.
1085	- **E-64. If the crew is aboard a derelict while the home ship stays lit** (Boarding & Salvage OQ-BS-15, AC-BS-80): the home ship's light and power terms **keep feeding the one world level** (AT-2; R2). A HOME-kind section is never dormant (Web Map & Transit), so its emitters and `power_use` are read every run like any loaded section's ("off-screen and unoccupied emitters count", EM:247); the lit-home term (766 mAU per tick at the F-25 placeholders) is part of the level the crew carries on the derelict. Switching home lamps off before a sortie is the player's lever. The locus can be a home section if its ledger leads (AT-14, Moment C).

For E-65's math, I'm tracing through the carry sequence: the tell opens at tick 318 referencing theta rather than theta_HOLD, level rises to ceiling during the tell since decay is suspended, then decays across the pod leg before the hop — trying to verify whether the stated arrival value of 4,511,793 mAU actually falls out of that decay calculation.

Then I'm checking a subtler question: does the hop void require the due run to land after the seat leaves the body, since if the breach timing falls during the walk to the pod rather than after departure, it hits the player on the derelict instead — which seems to be the intended design.

Moving to E-66, I'm confirming that cargo held at home carries no burden penalty, and that re-taking or returning an item before a rearm window closes cancels that rearm, then digging into how `pending_burden` gets set by an accepted BURDEN push and how the AT-10 cancel rule interacts with any CALM run occurring before the rearm deadline.

The real issue is that attributing a BURDEN push to a specific seat isn't actually tracked — `pending_burden` is just a global boolean, not per-seat, so the cancel logic can't tell which seat's push it's draining. This works fine for a single-seat MVP but breaks down in co-op, where one seat's carry state could wrongly trigger a cancel meant for another seat's item; I'm flagging this as a spec ambiguity to resolve later rather than something to fix now, since co-op is out of scope for MVP.

I also notice a mismatch: Controller's gate excludes DOWNED/DEAD states while Attention's AT-3 gate only checks for non-IN_POD, so Attention's wording is less complete per the ownership rule (registry shows attention-system owns `carry_burden_intake`, so Attention's gate should take precedence). Since Attention's own E-21 text confirms "a downed seat pushes nothing," I'll recommend tightening AT-3 to explicitly add DOWNED and DEAD exclusions for consistency with F-26 and decay-suspension behavior.

**Anti-pillar and neighbour guard rails the fantasy must not break.** (1) *Not a combat game:* Attention spawns nothing and defines no creature; the suppressant is a contract only, worded "repel or distract" and never "fight" or "kill"; a breach is survived or escaped, never won. (2) *Not intentional PvP:* Attention never gates or enables friendly harm; noise is attributed to sections for the locus only, never shown as blame, and no "who made the noise" readout exists. (3) *Not a freeform builder:* no placement bonus or penalty beyond what placed modules emit. (4) *No authored story, no win state:* no scripted breach; decay returns the level to the baseline and never below, and the survivable-dark floor holds at every ring, so a dark ship can always end a tell. (5) *The ship changes, you don't:* no adrenaline, speed, noise or control change in any phase (PCI:135, PCI:1010) and no camera reaction, shake or zoom (PIPE:151); the prose never says "your heart races", "tunnel vision" or "time slows". (6) *Nothing shows the level:* the UI Requirements section reads "none, by decision". (7) *The end of the tell is unreadable.* (8) *The sane palette:* iridescence only, never flesh or violet. ## Acceptance Criteria

*Source and ids.* Written from Core Rules AT-1 to AT-32, States and Transitions, Formulas F-1 to F-26 and Edge Cases E-1 to E-73 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: E-73 and AC-AT-134 to AC-AT-137 added)*. **Ids are stable:** `AC-AT-01` to `AC-AT-61` and `AC-AT-01a` are the ids the Core Rules already cite; `AC-AT-62` to `AC-AT-80` were added by the first draft; `AC-AT-81` and above close the qa-lead's gaps and the art-director's and audio-director's seeds. A criterion the qa-lead asked to split keeps its id with a letter (`06a` to `06e`, `49a` to `49c`, `54a`, `54b`, `57a` to `57g`). The tell-window criteria come first, as the index requires (IDX:34). Every number is a `[PLACEHOLDER]` from this GDD: a test reads the data file, never a literal, except where the number IS the point.

*Tags and gates (rigor full, project testing standard).* **(auto)** headless automated test: Logic or Integration evidence, `tests/unit/attention/` or `tests/integration/attention/`, BLOCKING. **(data-lint)** runs at boot or in a unit test over `assets/data/attention/`; it refuses boot, so it is BLOCKING in CI; every data-lint has a **negative fixture** (a data set that must fail). **(source-lint)** a static scan in `tools/ci/`, with a negative fixture. **(review)** a document or code review at a named point. **(manual)** a retained screenshot or capture in `production/qa/evidence/attention/[ac-id]-[rung|setting]-[date].png` plus an **art-director sign-off line**; Visual/Feel, BLOCKING (a capture that was discarded is an assertion, not evidence). **(playtest)** a playtest report in `production/qa/evidence/`, non-blocking. **(spike)** an engine or cost question answered by a measured spike. **(deferred: blocked on [system])** cannot run until that GDD exists; it stays an open item in the sprint-review blocker list and is never counted as a pass. Attention ships no screen, so no UI screenshot is owed (UI Requirements).

*Fixture glossary (so a tester without the GDD can run it).*

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| `TellAudit` | a DIAGNOSTIC-class ledger recording `(tick, caller, kind, section, tell_epoch, phase)` for every M17 RUPTURE, GOUGE and STRESS and every environmental M18 `apply_damage(..., EXOGENOUS)`; provisionally also every lethal act by a horror on a crew body (AT-15). A test fixture, written before Horror and Audio exist |
| Stub callers | test doubles that call M17 `deposit_trace` and M18 `apply_damage` with a chosen kind, section and tick, and a Horror double that can saturate `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` |
| Data files | `assets/data/attention/{intake, integrator, weights, baseline, tell, breach, presentation}.json` |
| `B_table` | rows ring 1 / 2 / 3 = 300 / 450 / 550 AU (rings 2 and 3 are test rows) |
| Dark fixture | `DARK_FLOOR_LOAD_W` 1,500 W, the EMERGENCY lamp (output 1000, reach 144) and `N_GLOW_DARK` (2, the shipping value under the valve-OPEN fallback; 1 under the closed-valve staging once ASK-G1 is accepted; 0 on the clean ship) |
| Home-ship fixture | three fixtures plus the EMERGENCY lamp, 1,900 W of draw, 766 mAU of light and power per tick |
| Oracle | a test-side arbitrary-precision integer model of F-1 to F-5 (a fixture, never sim code) |
| Roots | `tests/unit/attention/`, `tests/integration/attention/`, `tests/performance/attention/`, `tools/ci/` (source lints) |

### Gaps / untestable as written

1. **AC-AT-31** needs a named Graph read for the STRESS armed state; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* LS-19 now names `stress_active(section_id)` (`step_no < stress_until_step`), so the test accessor is retired once the Graph owner confirms it is the published read (OQ-AT-6).
2. **Deferred integration items** *(re-evaluated 2026-10-27 — design review)*: Web Map, Horror Entities, Modular Ship Assembly, Adaptive Audio & Tells and Sanity & Hallucination Rules are all Designed now, so AC-AT-46's notification half, 68, 72, 74 and 76 (Horror halves), 77, 78 and the audio half of AC-AT-47 are no longer blocked on a missing document: 77 and 78 were reviewed (results in their text), the others wait on implementation, and AC-AT-109 still waits for Sanity's fringe asset. Under the project evidence rule an Integration story still needs an integration test or a documented playtest, so every item that cannot run yet stays a named sprint blocker and is never counted as a pass.
3. **AC-AT-54b** has no budget until the technical-director sets it (0.05 ms is the primary's proposal, not a measurement).
4. **AC-AT-21's beat-count band** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* is now pinned from the integer model (19 / 20 / 23 at jitter +8 / 0 / −8; 19 to 23 under the real hash); the qa-lead's earlier band of 19 to 22 failed the −8 case.
5. **Player Fantasy's Moment A wording** no longer carries tick arithmetic (gate legibility ruling): it says only that an abort always costs the partial *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, the price of restraint chosen on purpose. The CR-TIMELINE numerics (480 + 114 = 594 ticks, six inside `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`) live in F-15b and are pinned by AC-AT-105, so a retune shows as a diff.
6. **F-25's occupancy sentence** was corrected (22.6 percent is inside the 15 to 35 percent calm-time target and above AC-AT-80's 20 percent floor).
7. **Lint negative fixtures** are listed where the qa-lead asked for them; the data-lints without one named (AC-AT-52 and AC-AT-64 excepted) take their fixtures from the first out-of-range row of Tuning Knobs.
8. **Not testable here by design:** the dB audibility margin of the bed (M2, a listening test owned by Adaptive Audio), beam strobing in sync with the cadence (E-20: the Controller adapter's debounce owns its criterion), and the world-side photosensitivity ceiling (the accessibility-specialist confirms).

findings.finding: The gate wording disagrees across the three documents. Attention AT-3, F-26 and the registry say the push runs unless `loco_state == IN_POD`. The Controller (PC-10, D.13) excludes `IN_POD`, `DOWNED` and `DEAD`. AC-AT-06f and E-21 say 'a DOWNED seat pushes nothing', which the AT-3 gate does not state. A second smaller drift: the gate says 'the holder's actor_section is in a non-home locus body' and the Controller says 'body_of_actor != HOME_BODY' (equivalent, but two spellings).
findings.fix: Make the gate `loco_state ∉ {IN_POD, DOWNED, DEAD}` in AT-3 (BURDEN row), F-26 (formula and the `carry_ref` row), AT-5, C33 and the registry expression. findings.section: Detailed Design AT-10 rearm cancel / States and Transitions L351

With two seats (VS co-op), seat A's recorded item held in the pod would be cancelled by seat B's unrelated BURDEN push on a derelict.
findings.fix: Define the test per seat from reads Attention already makes: `seat.carry_ref ∈ tell_carry_items AND actor_section(seat) in a non-home locus body AND loco_state ∉ {IN_POD, DOWNED, DEAD}` on a run with `pending_burden` set. Verdict: no BLOCKING defects. APPROVED stands, but the approval needs re-confirming because both files changed since the 2026-10-28 hashes, and I recommend the 11 follow-ups below before story work starts.

- **Gate mismatch:** the BURDEN gate in AT-3, F-26 and the registry omits DOWNED and DEAD, which the Controller and AC-AT-06f / E-21 exclude.

The remaining findings are stale gating text (C33, C35, OQ-AT-29, OQ-AT-37), pre-existing carry-overs (the E-38 air/heat contradiction, the `TELL_DRAW_LO` 780 range against the real 876 bound, the missing `void` token in the Audio GDD, stale status cells and cross-reference rows, Horror's `E_s`, the 2026-10-26 CD-GDD-ALIGN), and two missed R20 markers. Nothing found makes implementation wrong or impossible, and Attention's stories can be tested against doubles.
